title: Discrete dynamic survival analysis of epidemic case line lists
summary: Case line lists, which record dates of onset, recovery, and hospitalisation, are among the most granular data in infectious disease epidemiology and can provide insights into transmission dynamics. Dynamic survival analysis (DSA) fits a deterministic, differential-equation-based model to line lists to estimate parameters such as infectivity and the infectious period. Infectious periods are usually not exponential, and incorporating this into mechanistic models for line-list data often requires partial differential equation (PDE) schemes that can be difficult to implement and must be customised for each model, which may limit their use. Here, we propose Discrete Dynamic Survival Analysis (DDSA), a discrete-time DSA for case line lists based on difference equations. It matches calendar-day data directly without interpolation, and its log-likelihood is differentiable via forward-mode automatic differentiation, enabling off-the-shelf gradient-based samplers without model-specific numerical infrastructure. Non-exponential infectious periods are accommodated through a boxcar model or a discrete analogue of the "device of stages". We apply the DDSA method to three historical outbreaks of influenza A(H1N1), Ebola, and measles. DDSA estimates of transmission parameters were close to published analyses where these were available, an agreement that partly reflects shared modelling choices, and the method handles incomplete line lists with missing onset or recovery dates. Synthetic experiments show that recovery intervals identify the infectious period, while infection times and final size constrain R0 when the population at risk is known. Discrete DSA provides a simple, extensible framework for simulation and inference of infectious disease dynamics.
authors: Montes-Olivas S, Abbott S, Funk S, Gravenor MB, Frost SDW.

title: Phylogeography and transmission dynamics of the 2025-2026 Utah-Arizona measles outbreak: a retrospective genomic epidemiology study
summary:
Background:

Measles outbreaks are increasing in frequency globally as vaccine coverage decreases. During the 2025-26 Utah-Arizona border outbreak, identifying where and between whom transmission occurred was essential for directing control measures. However, epidemiological data alone are not sufficient to infer transmission patterns.

Methods:

As part of the local and state-wide outbreak investigation, we conducted amplicon-based whole genome sequencing on residual diagnostic samples from confirmed measles cases collected from June 15, 2025-April 30, 2026. We reconstructed viral dispersal across Utah using Bayesian phylogeographic analyses. We evaluated genetic distance thresholds for identifying recent transmission by comparing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based genetic clusters with known epidemiologic linkages. We then assessed pairwise exposures associated with genetically supported transmission linkage using logistic regression, accounting for network and spatial dependence between pairs.

Findings:

We generated 509 high-quality whole measles virus genomes from 913 patients. In 2025, most viral dispersal events (67.9%) originated in Southwest Utah and Mohave County, Arizona, where the first cases were reported. By 2026, most viral spread (60.5%) occurred outside of this area. A threshold of 0 SNPs identified epidemiologically linked pairs of individuals with a sensitivity of 77.4% and specificity of 92.3%. Household membership (odds ratio (OR): 219.10, 95% credible interval (CI): 112.66-325.53), participation in the same sport (OR: 15.19, 95% CI: 9.75-20.63), and attendance at the same school (OR: 51.5, 95% CI: 36.38-66.61) were independently associated with transmission linkage. Increasing distance between households was associated with reduced odds of linkage (OR: 0.46: 95% CI 0.44-0.48). Interpretation: Repeated introductions of measles virus from southwestern Utah seeded transmission elsewhere in Utah, with household, school, and sports exposures contributing to onward transmission. Validated genome-based linkage measures can complement contact tracing by helping public health teams identify likely transmission networks and prioritize investigation when resources are constrained.
authors: Marye A, Oakeson K, Lan Y, Warren JL, Francis D, Hicks L, Walter K.

title: Association between residence in flood-prone areas and incomplete childhood vaccination in Bangladesh
summary: Flooding events, closely linked to climate change and variability, can disrupt communities and health systems. Vaccination, a highly effective public health intervention, plays a crucial role in preventing child mortality worldwide. However, the relationship between flood-prone residence and early childhood vaccination remains underexplored. This study combines flood exposure data from the Global Flood Database with five waves of Demographic and Health Surveys (2004-2018) in Bangladesh, including vaccination histories for children under three years. Using geographic coordinates, households were matched to spatial flood data to identify whether children lived in flood-prone areas. Generalized Estimating Equations were applied, accounting for geographic clustering, to assess the association between flood exposure and incomplete vaccination overall, as well as by vaccine type and dose. The total sample included 19,021 children, with 12,930 of them being over 1 years old and included in the main analysis. Of those over one year, 16% were defined as living in flood-prone areas, and 84% were fully vaccinated. Children in flood-prone areas had a higher risk of missing the diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis (DTP; PR = 1.34, CI: 1.11-1.62) vaccine, the bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG; PR = 1.24, CI: 1.02-1.50) vaccine, and the oral polio vaccine (OPV; PR = 1.32, CI: 1.10-1.59) vaccines. Associations were not precise for the measles-containing vaccine (MCV; PR = 1.11, CI: 0.92-1.35) alone, nor for all four vaccines combined (PR = 1.09, CI: 0.91-1.30). These findings highlight that there is an association between residence in flood prone areas and certain vaccines, highlighting the importance of maintaining access to routine immunization services during floods, which are expected to increase with climate change.

title: Vaccination status and its association with complications among the patients admitted with measles in the dedicated measles hospitals, Dhaka, Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh is facing a major resurgence of measles, with more than 60,000 suspected cases and over 600 deaths reported between March and May 2026. Despite the growing outbreak, hospital-based evidence in Bangladesh remains limited regarding measles vaccination status and its association with clinical complications. To address this critical gap, our study aimed to assess the vaccination status and its relationship with the development of clinical complications. This cross-sectional study enrolled 260 children aged 2-72 months with clinically confirmed measles who were admitted to four dedicated measles treatment hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh, between 15 and 25 April 2026. Data on vaccination status, sociodemographic characteristics, feeding practices, nutritional status, clinical symptoms, and complications were collected through caregiver interviews and hospital records. Adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated; p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Among enrolled children, 74.6% were unvaccinated, 18.8% were partially vaccinated, and only 6.5% were fully vaccinated. In the multivariable model, age below 9 months (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.03-0.268, p < 0.001) was independently associated with lower odds of vaccination, while household income at or above the median (aOR 3.983, 95% CI 1.8-8.813, p = 0.004) was associated with higher odds. Complications developed in 31.1% of cases, with respiratory involvement being most common. Absence of exclusive breastfeeding (aOR 2.336, 95% CI 1.027-5.313, p = 0.043) and presenting with exactly three symptoms at admission (aOR 3.106, 95% CI 1.274-7.572, p = 0.013) were independently associated with complications. Unvaccinated children had markedly higher odds of complications than vaccinated children (aOR 5.729, 95% CI: 2.363-13.889, p < 0.001). The heavy burden of measles among unvaccinated children, shaped by socioeconomic disadvantage and suboptimal feeding practices, underscores the urgent need to restore immunization coverage and strengthen equitable health services in Bangladesh.

title: Measles-like hypermutation of a Newcastle disease virus drives fatal encephalitis during BCMA × CD3 T-cell-redirecting immunotherapy
summary: Newcastle disease virus (NDV or AOaV-1) is an avian paramyxovirus that typically causes only mild, self-limiting disease in humans. Here, we report fatal neuroinvasive AOaV-1 infection in a patient with multiple myeloma receiving maintenance therapy with teclistamab, daratumumab, and lenalidomide following frontline teclistamab-based treatment and autologous stem cell transplantation. Following rapidly progressive brainstem-cerebellar encephalitis and negative conventional microbiological testing, unbiased metagenomic RNA sequencing of a cerebellar biopsy identified AOaV-1 at high intraparenchymal abundance. Viral genome analysis revealed striking A-to-G and U-to-C substitutions selectively concentrated in the matrix gene, consistent with ADAR-mediated RNA editing. Long-read sequencing resolved two genetically distinct, independently hypermutated CNS haplotypes. Post-mortem analysis demonstrated widespread dissemination and continued viral diversification in multiple brain regions, whereas a peripheral urine sample contained a minimally mutated putative ancestral lineage. These findings support peripheral infection followed by CNS seeding and compartmentalized within-host evolution. The selective matrix-gene hypermutation closely parallels persistent measles virus infection in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, revealing a shared mechanism of paramyxovirus adaptation to the CNS. Profound immunotherapy-associated immune dysfunction may thus create niches enabling normally low-pathogenic zoonotic viruses to persist, evolve, and acquire severe neurovirulence.

title: Comparison of routine health-facility (KHIS) versus house-survey (KDHS) estimates of childhood vaccination coverage in Kenya: a cross-sectional study
summary: Reliable estimates of effective coverage of health interventions are essential for tracking progress towards health goals and informing policy decisions. In settings where routine health information systems are limited, population-based household surveys are frequently used as reference standards. This study compared national and sub-national childhood vaccination coverage estimates from Kenya's facility-based Health Information System (KHIS) and the 2022 Kenya Demographic Health Survey (KDHS) to assess concordance between the two data sources and to evaluate the suitability of routine data for programmatic decision-making. We analysed BCG, pentavalent 1, pentavalent 3 and measles-rubella 1 (MR 1) vaccination data reported by 8178 health facilities to KHIS between March 2020 and March 2022 alongside KDHS 2022 data from 3679 children aged 12-23 months. Coverage estimates were compared at national and county levels using a two-proportion z-test. Absolute differences in coverage were categorised as minimal (<5%), moderate (5-10%) and high (10+%), thresholds previously used in immunisation monitoring as reported by WHO and United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund coverage comparison. Nationally, KDHS coverage estimates were higher than KHIS estimates for BCG, pentavalent 1 and MR 1; the absolute differences were all <5% and statistically significant. For pentavalent 3, no significant difference was detected (0.38 percentage points; 95% CI -0.54 to 1.42). Sub-national discrepancies were substantially larger: minimal differences (<5%) were observed in only 15-21 of 47 counties depending on antigen, while high discrepancies (>10%) occurred in 9-14 counties. Only three counties showed absolute differences <5% across all four antigens; several counties showed persistent divergence across antigens. KHIS yields reasonably concordant national-level estimates of childhood vaccination coverage, but substantial and uneven county-level discrepancies limit its reliability for sub-national decision-making. A differentiated approach is warranted: KHIS can support national trend monitoring and may be usable in counties with demonstrated concordance, whereas counties with persistent divergence require continued survey-based validation and targeted strengthening of routine data systems. The two data sources should not be treated as interchangeable at county level.

title: Evaluation of a dual-intensity measles surveillance system in conflict-affected Borno State, Nigeria
summary: Maintaining measles surveillance in fragile, conflict-affected settings remains challenging due to insecurity, limited laboratory access and epidemic surges. Borno State, Nigeria, operates a dual-intensity surveillance framework combining laboratory-confirmed case-based surveillance (CBS-Lab) with epidemiologically linked outbreak reporting (CBS-Epi). We evaluated system performance, spatiotemporal surveillance patterns and operational constraints from 2020 to 2024. We conducted a programmatic surveillance system evaluation using the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention updated guidelines, assessing system attributes against WHO AFRO benchmarks. The evaluation used retrospective measles surveillance data (28 370 suspected cases) and a cross-sectional survey of surveillance officers assessing perceptual and operational domains (31/58; 53% response), supplemented by a contextual policy document review. Spatiotemporal alignment between surveillance streams was analysed using Spearman's rank correlation. CBS-Lab represented 6.1% (n=1725) of notifications, functioning as a sentinel subset with ≥98% completeness, a 47.8% positive predictive value and 88.4% specimen collection within 48 hours, though only 5% of cases met the <10-day turnaround standard.CBS-Epi (93.9%; n=26 645) maintained ≥99.8% completeness and captured epidemic peaks in 2021 and 2023, though representativeness was constrained by geographic inaccessibility in conflict-affected local government areas. No case-record overlap occurred between streams due to protocol design. Aggregate temporal (ρ=0.69) and geographic (ρ=0.65) co-variations were strong (p<0.001). Laboratory sampling intensity was inversely correlated with district case burden (ρ=-0.64; p<0.001), indicating risk-based prioritisation. Acceptability remained high despite insecurity, transport and funding constraints. Within the specific operational context of Borno State, dual-intensity surveillance enabled operationally useful epidemic intelligence and maintained mortality-reduction phase performance despite protracted conflict. These findings suggest that the pragmatic combination of simplified outbreak reporting and targeted laboratory confirmation may represent a feasible surveillance approach in comparable fragile settings, though contextual adaptation would be required.

title: Bridging microbiology and public health through simulation-based learning
summary: Within our synchronous, online global health-focused upper-level microbiology course, we find that students struggle to translate learning to real-world applications. For example, consider the recent measles outbreaks and major events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, which prompt many questions about how basic microbiological information is used by public health professionals. To address these points, we created a simulation-based curriculum that places students in an action role during an infectious disease outbreak. Our stand-alone curriculum walks through a historical measles outbreak that introduces outbreak investigation, community communication, and how these depend on microbiological knowledge. By using breakout groups, students have an opportunity to decide classifications, public messaging, and intervention metrics. We provide students with an outbreak investigation reference worksheet and interweave breakout rooms with didactic vignettes covering background information while revealing actual responses to outbreaks in conjunction with data obtained by responding scientists. Students synthesize material and apply it in real-time, allowing them to exercise critical thinking. Pilot testing in a small, upper-division, virtual classroom suggests that this curriculum has strong potential for increasing mastery of learning objectives and bolstering the relevance of microbiology and public health to popular media.

title: Strengthening catch-up vaccination delivery in routine health services for children under five in Western Kenya, 2022-2024
summary:
Background

Catch-up vaccination can close population immunity gaps, yet integration into routine immunization services remains limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Following Kenya's 2023 catch-up vaccination policy, we evaluated a multi-strategy intervention to strengthen systematic identification, eligibility screening, and delivery of missed doses within routine health services in Siaya County.

Methods

Over 12 months, five strategies addressing healthcare worker (HCW) capacity, vaccination documentation, defaulter tracking, immunization screening, and caregiver engagement were implemented in 55 public health facilities selected through stratified random sampling. Using a pre-post design, we assessed immunization uptake, missed opportunities for vaccination (MOVs), and system readiness. Baseline (November 2022-January 2023) and endline (October-December 2024) evaluations included facility assessments, HCW interviews, caregiver exit surveys among children aged <36 months with home-based records (HBRs; n = 658), and facility immunization register abstractions (n = 1650 children aged 12-23 months). Analyses accounted for sampling design, clustering, and used generalized estimating equations for HBR data.

Results

MOV prevalence among children visiting facilities for any reason declined from 94.4% to 20.9% (p < 0.001). Full immunization among children aged 12-23 months increased from 44.9% to 63.6% (p < 0.001), with uptake improving across antigens. Measles-rubella first-dose uptake increased from 51.5% to 78.0%, and second-dose uptake from 18.8% to 36.9% (p < 0.001 for both). Eligibility screening expanded from 60.6% to 86.8% of facilities (p = 0.012), defaulter tracking improved from 48.5% to 91.6% (p < 0.001), and HCW knowledge and confidence increased significantly.

Conclusion

The multi-strategy intervention was associated with fewer MOVs and improved uptake, suggesting that embedding catch-up vaccination within routine health services can strengthen immunization systems in decentralized LMIC contexts. Kenya's catch-up vaccination policy provided a framework for introducing catch-up vaccination into routine health services.

title: Susceptibility-weighted imaging findings in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: subcortical paramagnetic rim and deep gray matter changes
summary:
Background

Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration. With this study we aim to evaluate SWI changes in SSPE, with emphasis on the Subcortical Paramagnetic Rim (SPR) and deep gray matter mineralization, and to assess their association with parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy.

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI. T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods.

Results

SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001).

Conclusion

SPR and deep gray matter mineralization, are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.

title: Risk factors and aetiological agents of community-acquired pneumonia in children under five years in South Asia: A systematic review
summary: Pneumonia remains a leading cause of mortality among children under five years in South Asia, a region that, with sub-Saharan Africa, accounts for over half of the world's childhood pneumonia cases. To our knowledge, no prior review has jointly synthesised the risk factors and aetiological agents of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in under-fives specific to this region. This systematic review aimed to identify, critically appraise, and synthesise available evidence on the risk factors and aetiological agents associated with CAP in children under five years of age in South Asian countries. Following PRISMA guidelines, four electronic databases (MEDLINE, PubMed, Global Health, and Web of Science) were systematically searched for studies published between January 2000 and July 2024, with the search updated to January 2026. Quality assessment was performed using the Crowe Critical Appraisal Tool (CCAT), with only high-quality studies (≥75% score) included in the final synthesis. Data were synthesised narratively due to heterogeneity in study designs and outcome measures. From 1196 records identified and 747 studies screened, 16 met the inclusion criteria after quality assessment (8 on risk factors, 8 on aetiology), conducted across five South Asian countries (India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Bhutan). Young age (children 0-23 months), malnutrition (particularly underweight and wasting), and incomplete immunisation emerged as the most consistently identified risk factors across studies. Environmental exposures, including indoor air pollution, poor ventilation, and overcrowding, were significant contributors. Viral pathogens predominated in aetiological studies, with respiratory syncytial virus being the most frequently identified pathogen (mean detection rate 29.2%). Blood culture positivity for bacterial pathogens was generally lower (1.5-31.3%; below 13% in four of five studies), with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus most common among positive cultures. This systematic review demonstrates that childhood CAP in South Asia results from a complex interplay of modifiable host, environmental, and socioeconomic risk factors. Integrated interventions addressing nutrition, immunization coverage, household air pollution, and socioeconomic determinants are essential for reducing the substantial pneumonia burden among South Asian children.

title: Clinical consultation: The role of vitamin A in the management of confirmed acute measles infection
summary:
Purpose

Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, the rate of measles infection in 2026 is the highest in more than 3 decades. This clinical consultation explores the role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute measles infection and the challenges posed with this treatment in pediatric patients due to the limitations in currently available formulations.

Summary

The role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute, confirmed measles infection has been well established and is recommended by major medical organizations, including the World Health Organization and American Academy of Pediatrics. Despite the benefits that vitamin A has demonstrated in past studies, treatment with vitamin A remains difficult due to challenges in administration secondary to the limited formulations currently available in the United States. Multiple options exist to extract liquid vitamin A from capsules, but these methods are cumbersome and possess significant challenges.

Conclusion

Vitamin A treatment should be used in patients with acute, confirmed measles infection, after confirming that they are not at risk for drug interactions and have no symptoms of vitamin A toxicity if they were previously treated with vitamin A. A concentrated liquid formulation of vitamin A approved by the US Food and Drug Administration is needed to overcome current obstacles with administration of vitamin A in pediatric patients unable to swallow capsules.

title: Lampricide 3-trifluoromethyl-4-nitrophenol (TFM) impacts whole-organism oxygen consumption in non-target fishes
summary: The application of the lampricide 3-trifluoromethyl-4-nitrophenol (TFM) to streams infested with larval sea lamprey constitutes the backbone of the Sea Lamprey Control Program in the Laurentian Great Lakes, but native species have greatly varying sensitivities to TFM. Earlier work by D'Souza and colleagues revealed that the whole-animal oxygen consumption of larval sea lamprey responded in a dose-dependent manner to increasing TFM concentrations. We set out to determine (1) if TFM exposure leads to stepwise increases in whole-animal oxygen consumption in non-target fishes and (2) if exposure to lethal TFM concentrations leads to increases in oxygen consumption comparable to the animals' maximum metabolic rate (MMR). Using intermittent-flow respirometry, we tested three non-target fish species known to differ in their sensitivity to TFM: young-of-the-year lake sturgeon (sensitive), juvenile rainbow trout (intermediate), and juvenile smallmouth bass (resistant). We confirmed that all three species exhibit increases in oxygen consumption during exposure to increasing concentrations of TFM but found that the relationship between the MMR and oxygen consumption prior to death during lethal TFM exposure is complex and species dependent. While this complex relationship broadens the need for species-specific testing, it opens up interesting possibilities for both (1) in situ testing, e.g. through the deployment of riverside field respirometry systems to monitor real-time responses of both target and non-target species to TFM treatments, and (2) ex situ testing, e.g. through the establishment of less-lethal assays to determine TFM sensitivity under various species×temperature×water chemistry combinations.

title: Retrospective Analysis of the VAERS Database for Children One Year of Age
summary: In recent studies, novel candidate safety signals were detected for infants younger than 1 year of age for specific vaccines. Herein, the Vaccine Adverse Events Reporting System (VAERS) database was retrospectively examined for possible novel candidate safety signals for children one year of age. Novel candidate safety signals were detected for multiple vaccines. Two candidate manufacturing irregularities or possible unknown contaminants were identified associated with adverse event (AE) autism for VAERS nondomestic Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR II) vaccine lots from 1993 to 1995 and AE hyperpyrexia for nondomestic MMRV lots from 2019 to 2024. The candidate manufacturing irregularities were named alpha for MMR II and beta for Measles, Mumps, Rubella, and Varicella (MMRV) ProQuad vaccines. The hypothesized higher levels of alpha in the nondomestic data, MMR II appear to have been reduced or eliminated sometime soon after 1995; identification of alpha would contribute to future avoidance of possible associated AEs. Reduction of beta in the nondomestic MMRV vaccine is hypothesized to reduce hyperpyrexia and also higher pyrexia AEs not observed associated with domestic MMRV vaccine.

title: Acceptability and feasibility of measles vaccination, small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplementation, and their co-delivery among children aged 6–23 months in northern Nigeria: a qualitative study
summary:
ABSTRACT

Background

Undernutrition and infectious diseases form a vicious cycle that endangers child survival in low-resource settings, including in Northern Nigeria. The NutriVax-Measles trial was designed to evaluate a strategy combining preventive small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) distributions with community mobilization and routine immunization services for children aged 6-23 months to improve measles vaccination uptake. To inform future programs co-delivering nutrition supplementation and immunization services at scale, we aimed to assess the feasibility and acceptability of measles vaccination, SQ-LNS distribution, and the NutriVax strategy.

Methods

A qualitative study was conducted at the end of the trial using in-depth interviews (n=53) and focus group discussions (n=8) with key stakeholders: caregivers, health care workers, community health workers, and community representatives. Thematic analysis was guided by multiple conceptual frameworks.

Results

The majority of the participants expressed satisfaction with measles vaccines in both arms, and with SQ-LNS in the NutriVax arm, as they perceived the benefits for their children’s health. In both arms, community awareness sessions and previous experience of outbreaks were key to motivating caregivers to bring their children to healthcare centres. Although distance to health facilities was identified as one of the main barriers to accessing care, SQ-LNS was perceived as an important source of motivation to bring their child to the clinic where they subsequently received vaccination. All stakeholder groups emphasized the importance of community leaders’ support and targeted male sensitization to address the prevailing sociocultural norms. Additionally, improved service organization to reduce waiting time was considered crucial to enhance caregivers’ acceptability of the intervention.

Conclusion

Both measles vaccination and SQ-LNS provision were acceptable and feasible, supporting the NutriVax strategy within primary healthcare settings in fragile health systems. Successful implementation depends on sustained community sensitization, continued engagement of fathers and community leaders, and service delivery decentralized as close as possible to beneficiaries.

KEY MESSAGES

What is already known?

Co-delivering small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) with routine immunization is an effective strategy to improve vaccination coverage in Northern Nigeria. Yet, evidence on how vaccination and SQ-LNS are perceived, implemented, and experienced by stakeholders at health-care and community levels remains scarce.

What are the new findings?

SQ-LNS was an important source of motivation for caregivers to bring their children to health facilities, creating opportunities for vaccination. Persistent barriers to vaccination included socio-cultural misconceptions, gender norms, long waiting time and distance to health facilities.

What do the new findings imply?

Sustained community engagement, including targeted male sensitization, is important to improve measles vaccination acceptability. Successful implementation of co-delivery programs also requires well-organized service delivery, with services decentralized to health facilities as close as possible to beneficiaries, particularly to reduce travel distances and waiting times.

title: Parental Vaccine Refusal in Kazakhstan, 2023–2025: A Nationwide Register-Based Ecological and Spatial Analysis of Trends, Reasons, Data Quality, and Links with Measles and Pertussis
summary:
Background:

/Objectives: Kazakhstan experienced one of the largest measles epidemics in the WHO European Region in 2023–2024 and a pertussis resurgence in 2024, while documented parental vaccine refusals kept accumulating. Subnational, register-based evidence on refusal is lacking for Central Asia. We assessed trends, geography, structure and data quality of registered refusals and their ecological links with coverage and disease incidence.

Methods:

Nationwide ecological study of the official refusal register (20 regions; stocks on 1 January 2024–2026), surveillance reports and population data. We estimated prevalence per 100,000 with exact Poisson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and rate ratios (RRs), and applied χ² tests, Ward clustering, Moran’s I with local indicators of spatial association, Spearman correlation, negative binomial regression and Bland–Altman analysis.

Results:

Registered refusals rose from 39,792 to 66,240 (198.6 to 323.2 per 100,000; RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.61–1.65). Prevalence varied 23-fold between regions (39.8 in Turkestan to 932.4 in Atyrau) and increased significantly in 16 of 20 regions (Kostanay, RR 2.79). Personal beliefs dominated (62.1%); religious refusals (15.5%) clustered in the west and south (Moran’s I = 0.39, p = 0.011); media-attributed refusals grew by 39.8%. In 2024, refusal prevalence was associated with measles incidence (ρ = 0.55; incidence rate ratio 1.18 per 1/1000, 95% CI 1.03–1.34), and refusal explained 54.7% of pertussis cases. The register recorded 3.35–3.84 times more bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG) refusals than routine coverage reports, and 46 of 180 cumulative vaccine-specific counts decreased.

Conclusions:

Vaccine refusal in Kazakhstan is growing, regionally heterogeneous in magnitude and motive, and tracked measles burden during the epidemic. Reason-tailored regional strategies and a validated, individual-level electronic refusal register are needed.

title: Global Trends and Disparities in Maternal Mortality: A Longitudinal Multi-Country Analysis
summary:
Background and aims

Maternal mortality is one of the most significant global public health challenges and an important indicator of health-system performance and socioeconomic development. Although substantial reductions have been achieved since 1990, progress has slowed in recent years, and substantial disparities persist across countries and regions.

Methods

This longitudinal ecological study used country-level panel data from the Maternal Mortality Dataset compiled by Banerjee (2021), covering 182 countries from 1990 to 2021. Maternal mortality ratio (MMR), expressed as deaths per 100,000 live births, was natural-log transformed for statistical modeling. Human Development Index (HDI) group and continent were included as fixed-effect predictors, while linear mixed-effects models with country-specific random intercepts and random slopes for centered year were used to account for between-country heterogeneity and differences in temporal trajectories.

Results

Maternal mortality declined over the study period (β = -0.029, 95% CI, -0.032 to -0.026; p < 0.001). Compared with the High HDI group, countries in the Low HDI group had higher log(MMR) (β = 1.803, 95% CI, 1.458-2.147; p < 0.001), as did countries in the Medium HDI group (β = 1.042, 95% CI, 0.767-1.317; p < 0.001), whereas the Very High HDI group had lower log(MMR) (β = -1.004, 95% CI, -1.268 to -0.739; p < 0.001). Compared with Africa, log(MMR) was lower in America (β = -0.488, 95% CI, -0.813 to -0.162; p = 0.004), Asia (β = -0.838, 95% CI, -1.134 to -0.542; p < 0.001), Europe (β = -1.698, 95% CI, -2.067 to -1.330; p < 0.001), and Oceania (β = -0.953, 95% CI, -1.404 to -0.502; p < 0.001). Adding random slopes improved model fit (χ 2 = 8041.6, df = 2; p < 0.001), indicating heterogeneity in country-specific temporal trajectories. Marginal and conditional R 2 were 0.849 and 0.997, respectively.

Conclusion

Maternal mortality declined substantially between 1990 and 2021, but disparities persisted across HDI groups, geographical regions, and countries. The findings highlight the importance of socioeconomic and geographical context when interpreting global maternal mortality patterns and support context-specific approaches to further reduce maternal mortality.

title: Population level immunity to measles and rubella 5 years before and after the MR campaign in urban Vellore, South India
summary: India aims to eliminate measles and rubella (MR) by 2026. Despite >90% vaccination coverage reported in NFHS-5 and NFHS-6, assessing population-level immunity gaps remains essential to guide strategies for protecting vulnerable groups. We leveraged biobanked samples from two community-based serosurveys conducted in urban Vellore in 2013 and 2022, representing periods 5 years before and after the nationwide MR vaccination campaign. Age- and sex-stratified participants were tested for measles- and rubella-specific IgG antibodies using ELISA. Seroprevalence estimates were compared across surveys, and generalized additive models (GAM) were used to assess age-specific seropositivity patterns. Effective reproduction numbers (Re) for measles and rubella were estimated using mixture modeling approaches. A total of 1,029 samples from 2013 and 718 samples from 2022 were analyzed. Measles seroprevalence increased from 33%, 41%, 47%, and 48% in the 1-5, 6-15, 16-40, and >40 years age groups in 2013 to 77%, 71%, 89%, and 96% respectively in 2022. Rubella seroprevalence increased from 32%, 67%, 76%, and 73% to 93%, 84%, 93%, and 98% across the same age groups. No significant sex-based differences were observed for either infection. The estimated Re declined from 7.4 to 3.6 for measles and from 1.8 to 0.8 for rubella following the MR campaign period. Population immunity improved by 2022, particularly for rubella. However, lower measles seroprevalence among children aged 1-15 years indicates persistent immunity gaps despite high vaccine coverage, highlighting the need for continued surveillance and targeted strategies to achieve measles-rubella elimination in India.

title: Neurological Complications of Mumps
summary:
Abstract

Mumps is a vaccinepreventable viral illness that primarily affects the parotid glands but can also lead to neurological complications. During a community mumps outbreak in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India, between February and April 2025, we encountered several pediatric patients with significant central nervous system (CNS) involvement. We describe two children who presented with acute cerebellitis, meningoencephalitis with hydrocephalus, and aseptic meningitis in the setting of recent mumps infection. Detailed clinical features and shortterm outcomes are presented. All children improved with appropriate antimicrobial and antiviral therapy, immunomodulation in selected cases, and neurosurgical intervention when indicated. Our series demonstrates that severe mumpsrelated CNS disease continues to occur in partially immunized pediatric populations and can be associated with substantial morbidity. These observations highlight the importance of maintaining high measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine coverage, ensuring early recognition and comprehensive management of neurological complications, and strengthening surveillance for mumps outbreaks in India.

title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells
summary: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome<sup>1</sup>. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors<sup>2</sup>, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR-Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal-fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

title: Timing of antiretroviral treatment initiation and seropositivity to measles virus among children living with HIV in rural Zambia
summary:
Background

Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) reduces morbidity among children living with HIV (CHIV) but does not restore vaccine-induced measles immunity. Many CHIV now initiate cART before measles vaccination but the impact on measles seroprevalence is not understood. This study compared measles seropositivty between CHIV initiating cART before and after 9 months in Zambia.

Methods

This retrospective study was nested within a cohort study of CHIV and community-based studies in Macha, Zambia conducted from 2007-2020. Samples were tested for measles IgG antibodies by enzyme immunoassay from CHIV initiating cART at ages 0-8, 9-23, and 24-59 months and age-matched community-based controls. A cross-sectional analysis compared measles seroprevalence between CHIV groups after 6-12 months of cART and controls. A longitudinal analysis evaluated antibody concentrations from age 9 months through 48 months of cART and during the 2010-11 measles outbreak.

Results

In the cross-sectional analysis, measles seropositivity did not statistically differ after 6-12 months of cART by age at initiation (0-8: 30.8% [n=12/39]; 9-23: 37.0% [n=51/138]; 24-59 months: 26.6% [n=33/124]). Within CHIV groups, seropositivity was significantly lower than age-matched controls (63.5%, 75.7%, and 80.3%). Among 242 CHIV followed longitudinally, 46-56% had an antibody response, with estimated seroreversion in only 1.8-3.2 years. Among CHIV in 2010-11, 50% seroconverted or boosted with estimated seroreversion in 2.1 years.

Conclusions

Measles seroprevalence was low among CHIV, even when starting cART before 9 months of age, and the time to seroreversion was short. These findings support recommendations that CHIV, including infants, would benefit from periodic revaccination after immune reconstitution.

title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Clinical Outcomes of Vaccine-associated Urticaria: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Analysis of the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System Database (1990-2025)
summary:
Introduction

Urticaria is a commonly reported cutaneous adverse event following vaccination, which may range from mild self-limiting reactions to more severe hypersensitivity manifestations. Monitoring vaccine-associated urticaria is important for ongoing vaccine safety surveillance and pharmacovigilance. However, large-scale population-based analyses evaluating demographic characteristics, vaccine associations, onset intervals, and severity patterns remain limited.

Aim

The aim of the study was to analyze reports of urticaria in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) database between 1990 and 2025 and evaluate demographic characteristics, vaccine type distribution, onset intervals, temporal trends, and seriousness patterns.

Methodology

A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the VAERS database. Reports of urticaria submitted between January 1990 and March 2025 were included. The variables analyzed included age, sex, vaccine type, onset interval, and seriousness classification. Descriptive statistics were generated using frequencies and percentages, and comparative analyses were performed between serious and nonserious reports.

Results

A total of 61,996 urticaria reports were identified during the study period. Most reports occurred among adults aged 18-49 years and females. Most reports were classified as nonserious and occurred within the early postvaccination period. COVID-19 vaccines accounted for the highest proportion of reports, followed by influenza and measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Temporal analysis demonstrated a marked increase in reporting during 2021, followed by declining trends thereafter. Comparative analysis identified differences in demographic and clinical characteristics between serious and nonserious reports.

Conclusion

Urticaria is a frequently reported adverse event following vaccination, with identifiable demographic, temporal, and clinical patterns. Most reports were nonserious and occurred shortly after vaccination, although differences were observed between serious and nonserious reports. Continued pharmacovigilance and future studies incorporating detailed clinical data are needed to better understand factors associated with vaccine-related urticaria.

title: Assessment of the 2022 Constitutional Mismatch Repair Deficiency Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria Using the International Replication Repair Deficiency Consortium
summary:
Purpose

Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD) syndrome, caused by inherited biallelic mismatch repair (MMR) gene loss, is characterized by early-onset cancers and neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) features. Genetic heterogeneity of syndromes with replication repair deficiency (RRD) and non-RRD conditions (eg, Lynch syndrome (LS) and NF1, respectively) leads to diagnostic challenges. Seven diagnostic criteria (CMMRD1-CMMRD7) were established in 2022 incorporating germline results, ancillary tests, and clinical manifestation. This study reviews the use of these criteria in identifying CMMRD.

Methods

Individuals suspected of CMMRD referred to the International Replication Repair Deficiency Consortium in Toronto, Canada, had clinical manifestation, family history, germline, MMR immunohistochemistry (IHC) of non-neoplastic (NN-IHC) and tumor tissue, and LOGIC obtained to assess the diagnostic criteria.

Results

A total of 580 individuals were identified, with 159 excluded because of insufficient information resulting in 421 individuals assessed using the diagnostic criteria. Of these, 358 (85%) were classified as CMMRD/suspected CMMRD (n = 270), LS/likely LS (n = 78), or other hereditary conditions (n = 10). Sixty-three individuals could not be classified because of the lack of or discordant results. Of the 270 patients with CMMRD syndrome, 241 met the published criteria and 29 were suspected of CMMRD on the basis of fulfilling criteria with a discordant functional result or suspicious genotype/phenotype. CMMRD1-CMMRD7 criteria were all identified, with 57% (n = 137) fulfilling CMMRD1 criteria. Early-onset gliomas and GI cancers occurred in LS, POLE, TP53, and NF1. Digenic LS and concurrent hereditary cancer syndromes were identified.

Conclusion

The 2022 CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria provided a useful framework for establishing CMMRD syndrome and distinguishing it from similar conditions. A clinically meaningful subset remained difficult to classify despite suspicion of CMMRD. Refinement of CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria may address atypical presentation and discordant functional results. Limitations include incomplete availability of germline/functional testing, discordant/inconclusive results, and inherent referral bias to a specialized RRD consortium.

title: Childhood vaccination in Mali: Determinants and differences between conflict-affected and non-conflict regions from the 2023-2024 Demographic and Health Survey
summary:
Background

Armed conflict may disrupt immunization services and increase barriers to childhood vaccination. This study examined determinants of full basic childhood vaccination in Mali and assessed whether they differed between conflict-affected and non-conflict regions.

Methods

We conducted a secondary analysis of the 2023-2024 Mali Demographic and Health Survey, including 2859 children aged 12-23 months. Full basic vaccination was defined as receipt of Bacille Calmette-Guérin vaccine, three doses of pentavalent vaccine, three doses of oral polio vaccine (excluding the birth dose), and measles vaccine. Survey-weighted logistic regression models were fitted nationally and separately for conflict-affected and non-conflict regions. Interactions between conflict status and selected explanatory variables were tested.

Results

Full basic vaccination coverage was 51.87%. Coverage did not differ significantly between conflict-affected and non-conflict regions (50.08% vs 52.64%; p = 0.467), and conflict status was not independently associated with vaccination after adjustment. Antenatal care attendance and facility-based delivery were consistently associated with higher odds of full vaccination. In conflict-affected regions, media exposure and shorter perceived distance to health facilities were also associated with higher vaccination uptake. A significant interaction was observed between conflict status and distance to health facility (p = 0.01).

Conclusions

Childhood vaccination coverage in Mali remains suboptimal. Although overall coverage was similar across conflict and non-conflict regions, determinants differed by context, highlighting the need for tailored strategies to improve vaccine uptake.

title: Canada’s loss of measles elimination after 27 years: a mathematical modelling analysis of the five major provincial outbreak waves in 2025–2026
summary:
Background

Canada’s loss of measles elimination status in 2025 highlighted the vulnerability of populations with concentrated immunity gaps. Provincial incidence alone cannot readily distinguish relatively intense transmission within a small susceptible population from transmission involving a larger population. We quantified these differences across five provincial measles waves in 2025-2026.

Methods

We fitted a common susceptible–exposed–infectious–recovered (SEIR) model to weekly reported measles incidence for Ontario in 2025 and Alberta and Manitoba in 2025 and 2026. Mean latent and infectious periods were fixed at 10 and 8 days. We estimated the effective reproduction number ( R eff , 0 ), effective susceptible population ( S eff , 0 ), and profiled the initial infected number to evaluate province and wave-specific primary case model estimates. We calculate the initial exponential growth rate, doubling time, and peak full width at half maximum (FWHM) to characterize early epidemic growth and the duration of elevated incidence around each wave’s peak.

Findings

In 2025, Ontario’s effective reproduction number, R eff , 0 , was 1.9, with a model-estimated effective susceptible population, S eff , 0 , of 3,101 individuals, an initial doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and a peak FWHM of 12.3 weeks. Alberta had a similar R eff , 0 of 1.9, with S eff , 0 of 2,601 individuals, a doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and FWHM of 12.1 weeks. Manitoba had a lower R eff , 0 of 1.5 and S eff , 0 of 490 individuals, with a longer doubling time of 4.0 weeks and FWHM of 20.5 weeks. In 2026, Alberta’s R eff , 0 increased to 2.1 while S eff , 0 decreased to 383 individuals; doubling time shortened to 2.1 weeks and FWHM to 9.7 weeks. Manitoba’s R eff , 0 increased to 1.8 and S eff , 0 to 1,038 individuals, while doubling time shortened to 2.6 weeks and FWHM to 13.0 weeks.

Interpretation

Alberta’s smaller second wave combined the highest effective reproduction number with the shortest doubling time and peak duration, demonstrating that limited outbreak size can coexist with rapid transmission. Joint estimates of transmission intensity, epidemic pace, peak duration, and effective susceptible population provide complementary measures for comparing outbreaks and informing public-health planning. Together, these estimates provide a quantitative basis for distinguishing transmission intensity from the scale of susceptible involvement, supporting comparisons across outbreaks and informing the timing and scale of public-health responses for future outbreaks.

title: Ultrasensitive detection of neuronal DNA using genome-wide non-CG methylation patterns
summary:
Summary

Methylation-based liquid biopsies can identify the tissue origins of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). A major constraint on the sensitivity of these assays is the limited number of cell-type-specific CpG markers. Here we exploit the high abundance of non-CpG (CpH) methylation in neurons to enable ultrasensitive detection of neuronal DNA. We show that neurons carry 100-fold higher CpH methylation than other tissues, in which apparent CpH methylation largely reflects experimental artifacts. Using a computational criterion to identify cfDNA molecules carrying clusters of methylated CpA sites, we detect neuronal DNA at proportions as low as 20 parts per million. Analysis of 231 samples from 163 individuals revealed minimal neuronal cfDNA in the plasma of healthy subjects; elevated levels in patients with measles or acute neurological conditions; strikingly high levels in brain-dead donors, indicating extensive ongoing neuronal death; and the highest levels in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients in a neurological intensive care unit. These findings establish genome-wide, fragment-level analysis of non-CpG methylation as an ultrasensitive approach for blood-based monitoring of brain injury and disease.

title: Contact coverage, content of care and inequality in antenatal care and routine immunisation in rural Uttar Pradesh, India: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of household surveys and direct observations of community health sessions
summary: Community-based primary care aims to reduce geographic and opportunity-cost barriers in rural settings, yet population trends in coverage, content and education-related inequality are poorly described. In rural Uttar Pradesh (UP), monthly community health sessions (Village Health and Nutrition Days (VHNDs)) provide integrated antenatal care (ANC) and routine immunisation (RI). We describe long-term trends in coverage, content and education-related inequality, with direct observation of session readiness. We analysed repeated cross-sectional rural UP household survey data from National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-3 (births 2001-2006), NFHS-4 (2011-2016) and NFHS-5 (2018-2020). Outcomes included any and community-level ANC/RI, content-qualified ANC (Antenatal Care Quality (ANCq) ≥8), full RI among children aged 12-23 months and ultrasound use and caesarean birth as facility-dependent comparators. Education-related inequality was quantified using the Slope Index of Inequality and Concentration Index (CIX). Direct observations of 61 133 VHND sessions (2022-2023) described input readiness and observed ANC component delivery. Between 2001 and 2019, any ANC increased from 51.3% to 94.8% and content-qualified ANC from 3.3% to 53.3%. Any RI remained high throughout; full RI increased from 20.8% (2004) to 71.2% (2019). Gains were largest among women with no formal education. Relative inequality narrowed for every indicator and fell close to zero for services deliverable at community level (CIX 0.502 to 0.059 for ANCq, 0.269 to 0.018 for full RI), while remaining substantial for caesarean birth (0.394 to 0.257). Sessions showed high blood pressure and haemoglobin testing capacity and strong availability for key antigens, with lower but improving urine testing and measles-rubella vaccine supply. Content-qualified ANC and full immunisation improved markedly, with the largest gains among the least educated women and relative inequality narrowed for every indicator except caesarean birth. Where community-deliverable services have converged across education groups, the remaining gap lies in facility-dependent care. Further gains likely depend on referral, transport and surgical capacity rather than extending first-contact outreach.

title: Multiple Sclerosis and Viruses: « Liaisons Dangereuses »
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, multifactorial neurodegenerative disease with an aetiology that is still partially elusive. Several risk factors are associated with MS development including genetic predisposition and various environmental stressors; however, recently, viral infections have gained significant attention as a crucial environmental trigger. Despite the well-established link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS susceptibility, a single-pathogen model fails to clearly characterise the molecular cascades driving the disease, suggesting that the transition from infection to autoimmune response involves more than one viral agent. In this review we examine the speculation that the interactions among different neurotropic viruses could serve a collective causative role in MS, which is under-researched in the literature at present. We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

title: Influence of Intravenous Norepinephrine Administration on Melatonin Plasma Concentration in Awake and Anaesthetised Healthy Adult Volunteers
summary: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. Upfront Comprehensive Genomic Profiling in Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer: Real-World Implementation and Clinical Outcomes
summary:
Background

Biliary Tract Cancers (BTCs) are difficult-to-treat malignancies with limited therapeutic options and dismal prognosis. Upfront comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is recommended for advanced BTC to identify actionable alterations, but its real-world implementation remains underexplored.

Methods

In 2019, we implemented upfront CGP for advanced BTC at our institution. Molecular profiling results were reviewed within our institutional molecular tumor board when clinically applicable. Patients were followed throughout their disease course.

Results

A total of 80 patients with locally unresectable (n = 14) or metastatic (n = 66) BTC underwent CGP. Testing was performed on cytology material (6/80), tumor biopsies (38/80), or surgical specimens (36/80). In 59/80 cases (73.8%) testing was carried out prior to the beginning of palliative first-line treatment. In 42/80 (52.5%) cases, at least one clinically actionable genomic alteration was identified. The most frequent actionable alterations involved IDH1 (13.8%), FGFR2 (8.8%), ERBB2 (HER2) (5.0%), KRAS G12C (2.5%), and BRAF (1.3%). Alterations in DNA damage response genes were detected in 11/80 tumors, and 3/80 were dMMR/MSI-H. FGFR2 and IDH1 mutations were detected in ICC only, while HER2 alterations were more commonly detected in ECC and GBC. 11/42 patients with a clinically actionable alteration received targeted treatment during the disease course (1 first-line, 10 later lines). Among patients with an evaluable preceding systemic treatment line, treatment duration was longer with molecularly matched treatment than with the immediately preceding treatment line (p = 0.0391). 2/14 patients with initially unresectable BTC achieved secondary resectability during molecularly matched treatment.

Conclusion

Upfront CGP is feasible in routine clinical practice and identifies clinically actionable alterations in a substantial proportion of patients with advanced BTC. However, only a subset received molecularly matched treatment, highlighting a gap between molecular actionability and treatment implementation. Timely access to matched therapies remains critical to the clinical utility of precision oncology in BTC.

title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
summary:
Importance

Heart failure (HF) is a common condition with substantial geographical variation in its prevalence and underlying etiologies. Consistent and comparable data on the burden of HF within populations are needed to inform health system priorities.

Objective

To estimate the global burden of HF.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional study estimates disease burden using Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) methodologies to integrate multiple information sources. Data come from 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023 representing the global population with prevalent HF.

Exposure

HF and underlying etiologies.

Main outcomes and measures

Estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for the prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) for HF by age, sex, location, year, and underlying etiology.

Results

Globally, there were 56.0 million (95% UI, 49.9-62.2 million) estimated cases of HF in 2023. The estimated prevalence of HF generally increased with age for all locations. While ischemic heart disease and hypertensive heart disease were the 2 most common etiologies globally among older adults, there was substantial variation in etiological pattern by location and age. Congenital heart anomalies and rheumatic heart disease (RHD) were common etiologies in children and young adults, while the proportion of HF due to alcohol use peaked in middle adulthood. Location-specific estimates highlighted regions with higher burden of HF due to specific etiologies, including RHD (south Asia, east Asia, Oceania, southeast Asia, central sub-Saharan Africa, eastern sub-Saharan Africa, southern sub-Saharan Africa, and western sub-Saharan Africa), alcohol use (eastern Europe, Australasia, the Caribbean, and central Europe), and Chagas disease (southern, Andean, tropical, and central Latin America).

Conclusions and relevance

Heart failure is a significant global public health burden, and the impact is likely to increase as populations age. However, most HF etiologies can be prevented by interventions that reduce exposure to modifiable risk factors, such as elevated blood pressure, excessive alcohol consumption, and tobacco use. Etiology- and location-specific estimates can provide necessary information for public health officials to determine how best to prioritize interventions to reduce HF disease burden.

title: Climate-Related Disaster Adversity and PTSD-Related Outcomes Among Adolescents in Coastal Bangladesh: A Propensity Score Overlap-Weighted Analysis
summary:
Background

Climate-related disasters are important environmental stressors for adolescent mental health, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. However, evidence regarding post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD) among adolescents experiencing cumulative disaster adversity remains limited. This study examined associations between disaster adversity and PTSD-related outcomes among adolescents in coastal Bangladesh.

Methods

A cross-sectional school-based survey included 1697 adolescents from Grades 6-8 across three coastal upazilas between October and November 2025. Disaster adversity was assessed using an eight-item cumulative index, with ≥4 adversities defining elevated adversity. PTSD-related outcomes were assessed using the Child and Adolescent Trauma Screen-2. Physical activity and resilient coping were examined as exploratory correlates. Associations were examined using covariate-adjusted regression and propensity score overlap weighting with school-clustered robust inference.

Results

Elevated disaster adversity was associated with higher DSM-5 PTSD symptom severity (β = 5.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.33-10.09). In overlap-weighted analyses, elevated adversity was associated with a higher prevalence of probable PTSD on the basis of the ≥25 cutoff (prevalence ratio [PR] = 2.00, 95% CI 1.14-3.52), probable International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) PTSD (PR = 2.20, 95% CI 1.10-4.38), and probable ICD-11 CPTSD (PR = 3.00, 95% CI 1.04-8.67). The estimate for probable DSM-5 PTSD was PR = 2.01 (95% CI 0.99-4.06), whereas no association was observed with functional impairment (PR = 1.02, 95% CI 0.95-1.10). Physical activity was positively associated only with PTSD symptom severity (β = 2.37, 95% CI 0.39-4.36); resilient coping was positively associated with PTSD symptom severity and several probable PTSD outcomes. PTSD-related symptom burden was higher at greater levels of cumulative adversity, with little evidence of nonlinearity.

Conclusions

Greater cumulative disaster adversity was cross-sectionally associated with higher PTSD symptom severity and several probable PTSD-related outcomes. These findings support consideration of adolescent mental health within disaster preparedness and school-based psychosocial support, whereas longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships.

title: Measles resurgence in Italy: analysis of temporal patterns of viral transmission, surveillance performance, and vaccination coverage at national and regional levels, October 2023 to March 2025
summary: BACKGROUNDFollowing substantial progress towards measles elimination after the COVID-19 pandemic, Italy experienced a marked increase in measles cases in 2024.AIMOur aim was to describe measles epidemiology in Italy, October 2023-March 2025, and assess vaccination coverage, surveillance performance at national and regional levels, and temporal patterns of transmission.METHODSNumbers of measles cases and outbreaks were reviewed. Vaccination coverage and surveillance indicators were described at national and regional levels. Measles variants were classified by genotype and Distinct Sequence Identifier (DSId). Temporal transmission patterns of measles variants were assessed nationally and regionally to identify sustained transmission chains (≥ 12 consecutive months).RESULTSIn total, 1,311 measles cases were reported, with 178 outbreaks. Cases' median age was 30.9 years (IQR: 15.6-39.8); 601 were female (45.8%) and 710 male (54.2%). Only 3.1% (38/1,230) were fully vaccinated. In 2024, the first-dose vaccination coverage increased to 94.77% (95% CI: 94.70-94.84%) nationally, while second-dose coverage declined to 84.45% (95% CI: 84.35-84.55%). Among all cases, 12.1% (n = 158) were imported/importation-related, 64.1% (n = 841) were of unknown origin and 52.8% had DSId data available (n = 692), with high regional heterogeneity. Twenty-five measles variants were identified. One variant (D8-5963) showed sustained national transmission for over 12 months, meeting criteria for re-established endemic transmission, although no single region showed uninterrupted ≥ 12-month circulation.CONCLUSIONMeasles resurgence in Italy was marked by persistent immunity gaps, heterogeneous surveillance performance, and sustained national circulation of a D8 variant, indicating loss of near-elimination status. Strengthening vaccination strategies and enhancing molecular surveillance is urgently needed to restore progress towards measles elimination.

title: Measles resurgence in England: challenges in maintaining elimination, 2023 to 2024
summary: BACKGROUNDBetween October 2023 and September 2024, England experienced the largest measles outbreak in decades.AIMWe describe the epidemiology of the outbreak, burden on secondary care services and the factors that led to this resurgence.METHODSThe UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) conducts enhanced surveillance of all suspected measles cases in England. A measles line list was established using routinely collected notification, laboratory, demographic and vaccination information. Laboratory-confirmed cases were defined using serology and PCR. Incidence rates were calculated using mid-2024 population estimates. Severity was assessed through linkage with emergency department attendances, hospital admissions and length of stay.RESULTSMost of the 2,821 laboratory-confirmed cases resided in London (n = 1,283; 45.5%) and in the West Midlands (n = 710; 25.2%). Incidence was highest in London (14.1/100,000 population). Children under 10 years represented 58.6% (n = 1,653) of cases. Most cases (n = 2,609; 92.5%) were not vaccinated, and 63.0% (n = 1,776) lived in areas belonging to the two most deprived quintiles. Of the 2,788 cases that could be linked to hospitalisation data, 76.3% (n = 2,127) attended emergency care and 38.2% (n = 1,066) were admitted. Median length of stay was 2.0 days, seven cases received intensive care; one death was reported. Admissions were highest among infants aged < 1 year (51.6%, 165/320) and adults ≥ 30 years (47.2%, 195/413).CONCLUSIONThis outbreak reflects a shift towards endemic measles transmission in areas of high deprivation and low vaccine uptake in England. It underscores the importance of achieving 95% uptake with measles vaccine in all areas and communities to achieve and maintain elimination.

title: The effect of age at first dose of a measles-containing vaccine on measles humoral immunity: a retrospective cohort study, Canada, 2014 to 2016
summary: BACKGROUNDCanada eliminated measles in 1998; however, large outbreaks have been recently reported, and elimination status was lost in 2025.AIMWe aimed to estimate the effect of age at first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) on measles IgG concentration and seronegativity among two-dose recipients nearly two decades after vaccination.METHODSWe conducted a retrospective cohort study of 10,766 twice-vaccinated individuals tested for measles IgG from 2014 to 2016 in Ontario, Canada. We predicted measles IgG concentration and seronegativity using thresholds of < 275 mIU/mL, < 200 mIU/mL and ≤ 120 mIU/mL.RESULTSA 1-month increase in age at MCV1 (between 12 and 15 months) was associated with 13.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 7.1-20.8) higher predicted mean measles IgG concentration for females born after elimination and 9.2% (95% CI: 6.8-11.6) for females born before elimination. Depending on the seronegativity threshold and the measles elimination status at birth, a 1-month increase in age at MCV1 (between 12 and 15 months) was associated with lower odds ratio of seronegativity ranging from 0.74 (95% CI: 0.63-0.85) to 0.87 (95% CI: 0.57-1.27). Using the lowest threshold (≤ 120 mIU/mL) and the longest follow-up period (24 years post-MCV1), we predicted that 4.1% (95% CI: 2.7-6.1) of females vaccinated with MCV1 at 15 months of age would be seronegative, compared with 9.6% (95% CI: 7.4-12.3) of those vaccinated at 12 months.DISCUSSIONDelaying MCV1 to older ages (13-15 months) may result in an absolute decrease as large as 6% in the percentage of seronegative individuals, potentially increasing the likelihood of maintaining herd immunity.

title: Metamizole (dipyrone) versus ibuprofen for post-cesarean analgesia in women with preeclampsia with severe features: a quadruple-blind, randomized, active-comparator trial
summary:
Background

Adequate analgesia after cesarean delivery is a priority in women with preeclampsia, in whom opioid-sparing strategies are desirable. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) were historically avoided in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy because of a presumed effect on blood pressure, but randomized trials and meta-analyses have since shown no clinically meaningful blood-pressure effect, and current guidance supports their postpartum use when otherwise appropriate. Metamizole (dipyrone) is a non-opioid analgesic widely used in Brazil, Latin America, and parts of Europe, but its regulatory status varies internationally. It is not approved in the United States, and agranulocytosis is a recognized rare but potentially serious adverse reaction. European regulatory guidance also advises against its use during breastfeeding. No randomized trial has directly compared metamizole with an NSAID after cesarean delivery in women with preeclampsia.

Objective

To compare metamizole and ibuprofen for analgesic effectiveness and short-term safety, with particular attention to blood pressure trajectory and renal function, after cesarean delivery in women with preeclampsia with severe features.

Study design

Quadruple-blind (participant, care provider, investigator, outcome assessor), randomized, active-comparator, phase 4 trial at a tertiary maternity hospital in northeastern Brazil. Seventy-four women received oral metamizole 1 g or ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours for up to 5 days, with intravenous tramadol available as rescue analgesia. Co-primary outcomes, as prospectively registered, were postoperative pain-categorized as mild, moderate, or severe by visual analogue scale (VAS)-and acute kidney injury (AKI). Continuous VAS, the D1-to-D2 mean reduction in VAS, the clinically interpretable threshold VAS ≥4, the Faces Pain Scale-Revised, peri-incisional pressure pain thresholds by algometry, rescue analgesia, serial blood pressure, hypertensive episodes, laboratory values, satisfaction, and length of stay were secondary or supportive outcomes. Effects were estimated with risk differences, risk ratios, exact tests, Hodges-Lehmann differences, standardized effect sizes with Holm correction, and linear mixed-effects models.

Results

Thirty-eight women were allocated to metamizole and 36 to ibuprofen. The registered three-category pain distribution did not differ between groups on day 1 (exact P=.45) or day 2 (exact P=.55). Median VAS was 4 (IQR 2-5) in both groups on day 1 and 2 (IQR 2-4) versus 3 (IQR 2-4) on day 2; the mean D1-to-D2 VAS reduction was 1.0 (SD 2.1) versus 0.6 (SD 2.4), with a mean between-group difference in reduction of 0.36 points (95% CI -0.70 to 1.42; P=.50). Rescue analgesia on day 1 was required by 18.4% versus 38.9% (risk difference -20.5 percentage points, 95% CI -39.1 to 0.1). AKI occurred in 3 of 38 (7.9%) versus 1 of 36 (2.8%) (risk ratio 2.84; 95% CI 0.31-26.08; Fisher P=.62; risk difference +5.1 percentage points, 95% CI -7.4 to 18.2). Linear mixed-effects models showed no group-by-time interaction for systolic (P=.14) or diastolic (P=.18) blood pressure; robust GEE sensitivity analyses were concordant. Severe hypertensive episodes were rare in both arms.

Conclusion

In this randomized trial, no clear between-group difference was detected in postoperative pain or blood-pressure trajectory. The trial was not designed as an equivalence or non-inferiority study. AKI was numerically more frequent with metamizole, but the estimate was highly imprecise; comparative renal safety remains uncertain and requires adequately powered studies.
