Two-Dose Measles-Containing Vaccine (MCV1 and MCV2) Completion and Associated Factors Among Children Aged 24-59 Months in Soroti City, Uganda: A Cross-Sectional Study
summary: This study aimed to determine the measles immunization completion rate, defined as receipt of both the first (MCV1) and second (MCV2) doses of measles-containing vaccine, and associated factors among children aged 24-59 months in Soroti City, Northeastern Uganda. A quantitative analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in Soroti City between November 2025 and January 2026. Multi-stage cluster random sampling was employed to select 325 children aged 24-59 months from households in eight villages across two divisions of Soroti City. Data were collected through face-to-face interviewer-administered questionnaires targeting caregivers. Immunization status was verified using child health cards and, where cards were unavailable, caregiver recall. Data were analyzed using Stata version 15.0, with descriptive statistics, bivariate chi-square tests, and multivariate logistic regression performed at a significance level of p < 0.05. The measles immunization completion rate was 76.6% (95% CI: 71.7-80.9%). Six variables were significantly associated with completion at the bivariate level (p < 0.05) and were entered into the multivariable model: birth order, caregiver occupation, household income, ANC attendance, outreach service availability, and vaccine safety perception. At multivariate analysis, factors independently associated with measles immunization completion were birth order of three and above (AOR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15-0.93; p = 0.034), unemployed caregiver occupation (AOR = 2.88; 95% CI: 1.50-5.52; p = 0.002), household income of 200,000-<500,000 UGX (AOR = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.15-0.61; p = 0.001), antenatal care attendance of more than six visits (AOR = 5.77; 95% CI: 1.86-17.93; p = 0.002), availability of outreach services (AOR = 3.82; 95% CI: 1.90-7.70; p < 0.001), and agreement that measles vaccines are safe (AOR = 16.27; 95% CI: 2.83-93.64; p = 0.002). Attendance of 3-6 ANC visits and household income of ≥500,000 UGX were associated with completion at the bivariate level but did not remain statistically significant after adjustment. Measles immunization completion among children aged 24-59 months in Soroti City was 76.6%, substantially higher than Uganda's national MR2 uptake of 28% reported for the 2023/2024 financial year, but still below the WHO-recommended 95% threshold; because the national and study estimates refer to different periods and populations, this comparison should be interpreted as indicative rather than a direct benchmark. Outreach service availability, vaccine safety perception, ANC attendance, caregiver occupation, household income, and birth order were the factors most strongly associated with completion in this setting. Strengthening outreach services, integrating immunization counselling into ANC, addressing caregiver concerns about vaccine safety, and paying closer attention to households with several children are programmatic implications suggested by these associations, though intervention effectiveness was not directly tested in this cross-sectional study.

title: Oncolytic virotherapy for cancer: biological mechanisms, clinical advances, and future perspectives
summary: Oncolytic virotherapy has emerged as a promising cancer treatment that combines selective tumor destruction with potent stimulation of antitumor immunity. Unlike conventional therapies, oncolytic viruses (OVs) preferentially infect and replicate within malignant cells while sparing normal tissues, leading to direct tumor lysis and the release of tumor-associated antigens, pathogen-associated molecular patterns, and damage-associated molecular patterns that activate both innate and adaptive immune responses. Advances in molecular virology and genetic engineering have transformed naturally occurring viruses into programmable therapeutic platforms capable of delivering immunomodulatory payloads that enhance antitumor efficacy and remodel the tumor microenvironment. Multiple DNA- and RNA-based viral platforms, including herpes simplex virus, adenovirus, vaccinia virus, reovirus, measles virus, Newcastle disease virus, vesicular stomatitis virus, and coxsackievirus, are currently under clinical investigation, with regulatory approval of talimogene laherparepvec (T-VEC) and G47Δ providing important proof of clinical feasibility. Increasing evidence indicates that OVs can convert immunologically "cold" tumors into "hot" tumors, thereby improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors and other therapeutic modalities. Consequently, oncolytic virotherapy has become an attractive component of combination strategies involving immunotherapy, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapies, and cellular therapies. Nevertheless, several challenges continue to limit its broader clinical application, including antiviral immune clearance, inefficient systemic delivery, restricted intratumoral spread, tumor heterogeneity, manufacturing complexity, and the lack of robust predictive biomarkers. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the biological foundations of oncolytic virotherapy, viral engineering strategies, mechanisms of tumor selectivity, direct oncolysis, immunogenic cell death, and immune remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. It further summarizes the major oncolytic virus platforms, recent preclinical and clinical advances, emerging combination strategies, current translational challenges, and future directions expected to advance precision oncolytic virotherapy and expand its role in modern cancer treatment.

title: Associations between parental generative artificial intelligence health-advice use and child vaccination uptake in Japan: an exploratory cross-sectional study
summary:
Background

Parents increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (AI) for health information, but evidence on parental AI use and childhood vaccination is limited. We examined exploratory associations between regular parental AI health-advice use and childhood vaccination in Japan.

Methods

This cross-sectional study analyzed 2025 nationwide survey data from children aged 1 to 17 years and parents, with a linked 2023-2025 sub-analysis. The exposure was regular parental use of generative AI for health advice at least a few times per month. Outcomes were age-appropriate measles-rubella (MR) vaccination and any mumps, influenza, or coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) with parent-level clustering and covariates.

Results

Among 8282 children and 5170 parents, 1278 (15.4%) had regular AI health-advice users as parents. AI use was not associated with age-appropriate MR vaccination (aPR 1.02; 95% CI 0.97-1.09), but was associated with three vaccines. The adjusted rates were 76.6 versus 72.7% (aPR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10) for mumps, 56.7% versus 49.0% (aPR 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.24) for influenza, 40.6% versus 30.9% (aPR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19-1.45) for COVID-19. The COVID-19 association was strongest among parents younger than 30 years (aPR 2.58; 95% CI 1.90-3.50; P for interaction < 0.001). In the linked sub-analysis, these associations persisted after adjustment for an available 2023 household-level prior vaccination marker and attitudes.

Conclusions

Regular parental use of generative AI for health advice was associated with mumps, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccination, but not with age-appropriate MR vaccination. These exploratory, cross-sectional findings are observational associations. They may reflect digital health engagement, health information seeking, socioeconomic differences, or favorable attitudes, rather than vaccine-specific AI advice.

title: Rapid Differentiation of Vaccine and Wild-Type Measles Virus During an Ongoing Outbreak using a new molecular assay
summary:
Background

Differentiating wild and vaccine measles virus (MeV) strains is critical for appropriate healthcare response during outbreak vaccination campaigns. Sequencing, the current standard, is expensive, time-consuming, and limited to specialized laboratories. We developed and implemented a novel differential MeV RT-qPCR assay to address these challenges, which we describe herein.

Methods

We designed a differential two-step assay; the first step, termed MRRV, distinguishes between rubella, wild MeV, and vaccine MeV. The second, termed "MeV differential", differentiates between genotypes A (vaccine), B and D.

Results

The assay detects 10-50 copies per reaction and accurately classifies weak clinical samples (Cq > 32), with 100% accuracy, compared with the N gene sequencing gold standard. Evaluated on over 4,000 clinical samples retrospectively and during the 2025-2026MeV outbreak in Israel, the assay revealed that ∼9% of tested originated from vaccine strain. Among tested municipalities, those running active vaccination campaigns had significantly higher vaccine strain detections (>10 cases each) than those with routine vaccination (1-2 cases). Retrospective analysis of samples from 2018-2024 identified a mix of B and D strains. The novel assay successfully identified double infection cases (exposure to a wild strain shortly before or after vaccination).

Conclusion

The novel assay proved useful both as a diagnostic tool that enables focused, efficient healthcare response, and as an epidemiological tool that provides valuable information in real-time. This assay is faster, cheaper and more amendable for high throughput testing, compared with the gold-standard sequencing classification.

title: Generating Insights Into (Mis)Information About Measles Vaccination in Amsterdam Through Social Listening, the Netherlands, 2024
summary:
Suboptimal vaccination coverage for Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) and increases in measles cases in the Netherlands prompted innovation to support informed vaccine decision-making. Through an iterative approach, this pilot implemented and evaluated social listening in the context of a local public health authority, namely Public Health Service Amsterdam. As a pilot study, we generated insights in measles vaccination. First, potential online and offline social listening data sources were identified. Second, in August-September 2024, data on measles vaccination discourse were gathered. Third, quantitative and qualitative (thematic) analyses were applied to generate insights, and risk assessment was conducted to determine their potential impact on health attitudes. We identified twenty sources for social listening. Six were selected for monitored based on feasibility and relevance. These sources were Public Health Service Amsterdam internal observations (public health professionals’ observations, source and contact tracers’ calls, and press inquiries) and three social and news media sources: Coosto, LexisNexis, and Google Trends. Results revealed diverse health beliefs, risk perceptions, concerns, and misinformation shaping vaccination attitudes. Prevalent themes included false claims on effectiveness, causes and effects of measles (vaccination), practical concerns and questions, and positive sentiments. Online and offline social listening enabled insight generation into public health perceptions during an anticipated measles outbreak. This approach is essential for understanding public needs, addressing misinformation, and informing targeted communication during public health challenges.

Author Summary

Declining vaccination coverage for measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) in the Netherlands and concerns about a potential rise in measles cases prompted efforts to better understand public attitudes toward vaccination. To support informed decision-making, we tested a new approach called social listening within the Public Health Service Amsterdam. Social listening combines information from multiple, different sources, both online (e.g. social media, news, and search trends) and offline sources (such as source and contact tracers and reports from public health professionals) to understand what people are saying and exposed to regarding a specific health topic in real time. In this pilot study, we identified and monitored selected data sources during August and September in 2024. We manually analyzed this information to identify common questions, concerns and misinformation about measles vaccination. Combining these insights revealed a wide range of views describing vaccination attitudes, information gaps and themes of distrust and misinformation, but also positive sentiment. This approach provided timely insight into emerging and entrenched public perceptions and showed that social listening can effectively be implemented within a local health service. These findings highlight the potential of integrating social listening into routine public health practice to support responsive and evidence-informed communication strategies.

title: Case Study on Formulating a Multidose Lyophilized Measles-Rubella (MR) Vaccine Candidate for Local Manufacturing in Africa: Lab-Scale Results and Lessons Learned for Future Technology Transfer
summary: Background/Objectives: Local manufacturing of Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccines is part of a multifaceted approach to improve vaccine accessibility in Africa, yet process development and technology transfer challenges remain for large-scale production of viral bulks and lyophilized drug product. This case study describes lab-scale formulation development of a multidose, lyophilized MR vaccine candidate, leveraging the availability of concentrated bulks of Measles (MeV) and Rubella (RuV) produced in MRC-5 cells by a new bulk manufacturing process. Methods: Formulation studies utilized both high-throughput RT-qPCR viral infectivity assays and standard lyophilization measurements. The off-patent, publicly available formulation composition of a single-dose, lyophilized trivalent MMR vaccine was evaluated as a starting point to develop a multidose, bivalent lyophilized MR vaccine candidate. To identify optimized conditions, various formulation (e.g., human serum albumin, viral bulk volume), drug product (e.g., vial size, fill volume), and lyophilization (e.g., freezing rate, primary/secondary drying cycle) parameters were evaluated to lower costs and assess MR stability during lyophilization, storage, and reconstitution. Results: Real-time and accelerated stability studies were conducted with four variations of the top candidate MR formulation, filled into primary packaging selected for technology transfer and lyophilized in both lab- and pilot- scale freeze-dryers. An optimized five-dose MR vaccine formulation with 5% (v/v) bulk and 95% (v/v) stabilizer solution, filled at 2X and reconstituted to 1X concentrations, demonstrated promising stability profiles and cost reduction potential. Stability profiles at 2-8 °C were used to estimate the MR release doses needed to ensure the required expiry doses at end of shelf-life. Conclusions: Results are discussed, along with recommendations for future work, in the context of the analytical, formulation, and lyophilization challenges encountered during lab-scale development of a candidate multidose, lyophilized MR vaccine dosage form targeted for technology transfer and large-scale local production in Africa.

title: Integrated Molecular Classification of Endometrial Cancer: Impact on Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Clinical Management-A Systematic Review
summary:
Objective

To systematically review the literature on the impact of integrated molecular classification of endometrial cancer on diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and clinical management.

Methods

A systematic search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane Library (January 2013-December 2025), following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We included original studies, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and cost-effectiveness analyses applying TCGA molecular classification or its surrogate classifiers (ProMisE, TransPORTEC). Data were extracted on subtype distribution, survival outcomes, hazard ratios, stage migration, and therapeutic implications.

Results

Fifty studies were included. Of these, 13 provided data on molecular subtype distribution (comprising 3527 patients), 8 reported survival outcomes, and 7 reported hazard ratios. The weighted subtype distribution from the 13 studies was as follows: POLEmut 8.9%, MMRd 25.8%, p53abn 16.7%, and NSMP 48.2%. POLEmut was associated with an excellent prognosis (5-year overall survival >95%, hazard ratio <0.5), while p53abn represented the poorest prognosis group (5-year disease-free survival 33-58%, hazard ratio >2.0). p53abn was the only independent risk factor for peritoneal (odds ratio 8.54) and vaginal (odds ratio 6.51) recurrence. Molecular classification modified risk group assignment in 6-33% of patients and improved prognostic discrimination of the 2023 FIGO staging system. Therapeutic implications include treatment de-escalation in POLEmut, immunotherapy in MMRd, and intensive chemotherapy in p53abn. Barriers to implementation include access to POLE sequencing and cost-effectiveness.

Conclusions

Integrated molecular classification is an essential tool for prognostic stratification and treatment personalization in endometrial cancer. Molecular subtypes demonstrate clearly differentiated prognostic profiles and recurrence patterns, justifying their systematic incorporation into clinical practice and international guidelines.

title: Hemagglutinin and fusion proteins precede measles virus ribonucleoproteins and marshal cell-to-cell spread in airway epithelium
summary: Measles virus (MeV) is the most contagious human respiratory pathogen. To understand how it spreads in the airways, we infected well-differentiated primary cultures of human airway epithelial cells (HAE). We discovered that the MeV attachment protein (hemagglutinin, H), the fusion (F) protein, and the assembly organizer protein (matrix, M) reach newly infected cells ahead of, and independently from, the replicative complex proteins. To characterize the mechanisms of MeV spread, we generated a replication-deficient adenoviral vector expressing the MeV M, F, and H proteins in a doxycycline-inducible manner. This viral vector formed infectious centers that preserved epithelial function like those from MeV infection. To further dissect this process, we generated Ad vectors expressing individual MeV proteins, termed Ad-M, Ad-F, and Ad-H. Transduction of HAE with single, double, and triple Ad vector combinations revealed that Ad-F and Ad-H are necessary and sufficient to form MeV-like infectious centers. MeV enters and spreads within airway epithelia via H protein binding to adherens junction protein, nectin-4. To disrupt spread, we introduced the point mutation HY543A, a mutation previously described to inhibit nectin-4 binding, in the Ad-H vector. Co-transduction of Ad-F and Ad-HY543A did not result in MeV-like infectious center formation. Finally, we assessed whether the MeV-related paramyxovirus Nipah (NiV) attachment and fusion proteins (G and F, respectively) support cell-to-cell spread. Co-transduction of HAE with Ad-NiV-G and Ad-NiV-F did not result in infectious center formation, suggesting that decoupling of the membrane fusion apparatus function from replication is a unique feature of the MeV envelope glycoproteins.IMPORTANCEMeasles virus is a highly contagious pathogen. We characterized a mechanism by which measles virus spreads rapidly through the cells that line the human airway in an ex vivo model. We show that the proteins of the viral membrane fusion apparatus, hemagglutinin (H) and fusion (F), move independently from and reach newly infected cells before the proteins of the replicative complex. Thus, viral protein spread is assembled and arranged in order (i.e., marshaled). Using adenovirus-based vectors, we show that co-expression of H and F proteins promotes rapid sequential spread to multiple cells and the formation of infectious centers. Further elucidation of the mechanism of measles virus amplification and cell-to-cell spread within the lung may help explain its highly contagious nature.

title: An evaluation of the performance and usability of a measles IgM rapid diagnostic test within the Uganda national surveillance program using capillary blood and oral fluid samples
summary: Performance of a prototype measles IgM rapid diagnostic test (RDT) was evaluated during suspected measles outbreaks in Uganda.Oral fluid (OF), capillary blood (CAP) and serum samples were collected from participants. OF and CAP were tested using the RDT at patient contact, while usability was assessed through questionnaires administered to health workers, patients, and guardians. Residual OF and IgM-positive RDTs from OF testing underwent measles qRT-PCR at Uganda Virus Research Institute. RDT performance was compared with Siemens anti-measles IgM ELISA performed on sera and with true measles cases, defined as measles ELISA IgM-positive and/or OF RT-PCR positive.Compared to ELISA, RDT sensitivity and specificity were 97.9% (95% CI: 93.7%-99.3%) and 91.7% (95% CI: 84.7%-95.7%) for CAP, and 96.7% (95% CI: 92.2%-98.6%) and 88.0% (95% CI: 80.7%-92.8%) for OF, respectively. title: Predicting Measles Vaccination Defaulting in Uganda and Kenya: Comparative Evaluation of Custom Soft Voting and TabNet Stacked Ensemble Architectures
summary:
Background

Measles is a major cause of death among infants despite free routine immunization (RI) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Vaccination defaulting contributes to measles outbreak occurrences. Conventional immunization defaulter identification methods are expensive to implement, prone to data falsification, reactive, and overestimate uptake. Several machine learning studies leveraged the use of child and maternal characteristics as predictors of immunization defaulting, overlooking community, demographic, and socioeconomic factors. Similarly, there is limited research regarding the use of interpretable deep learning and advanced ensemble methods to improve model performance in predicting RI defaulters and establishing significant predictors at the national level in the LMIC context, like Uganda.

Objective

This study predicts infants at a risk of defaulting on measles vaccination in Uganda and Kenya using advanced ensemble learning architectures.

Methods

The study benchmarked classical and deep learning models using Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) datasets (2016-2022) with child, maternal, community, social-economic, and demographic characteristics as predictors. The robust modeling pipeline began with feature selection according to the literature and the expert domain. It was followed by vaccination eligibility, missing value handling, and feature elimination using the phi-k correlation framework. To mitigate class imbalance, synthetic minority over-sampling technique for nominal continuous features was used in a training pipeline after the RobustScaler. Nine baseline classifiers, including Tabular Network (TabNet), multilayer perceptron (MLP), random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), adaptive-boosting (AB), among others, underwent stratified k-fold cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization via grid search. Custom soft voting was evaluated alongside TabNet stack architecture for superior ensemble prediction. Models were evaluated for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Model explainability was decoded using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), while Streamlit and SQLite formed the tool architecture.

Results

The proposed TabNet+GB+RF custom soft voting achieved significant, nonrandom performance over tuned base models with an F1-score of 0.7111, area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8847 for Kenya. Conversely, for Uganda, the TabNet hybrid ensemble (GB+RF+ AB→TabNet) was the best with AUC of 0.8862 and F1-score of 0.6756, which was statistically insignificant. SHAP identified child's age and vitamin A1 as universal key predictors in both countries; others varied. In Kenya, time to water source, respondents' education, district lived previously, and current district were the most influential global features, respectively. In Uganda, Polio inactive, Pentavalent3, current district, and respondents' education were the most influential factors to defaulting, respectively.

Conclusions

The proposed advanced ensemble learning models improved the classification of measles vaccine defaulters compared to individual models. The study recommends distinct country-tailored strategies. In Kenya, outreaches are recommended to areas with low literacy, distant water sources, and mobile populations. Conversely, in Uganda, the study recommends reminders to avoid missing preceding vaccines and outreaches to high-default districts.

title: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis after Measles Outbreaks, the Philippines, 2007-2022
summary: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a delayed, almost uniformly fatal complication of measles. The Philippines had measles outbreaks in 2010-2011, 2013, and 2018-2019; the last was the largest in the World Health Organization Western Pacific Region. Published SSPE data from the Philippines end in 2015. We reviewed all 20 children admitted with SSPE to a tertiary pediatric hospital in Quezon City during 2007-2022 and estimated year of measles infection. Median patient age was 6.2 years at hospital admission and 0.7 years at reported measles illness. Five (25.0%) of 20 admissions occurred in 2022, and estimated infection dates placed 4 patients within the 2018-2019 outbreak; all were admitted during 2020-2022. Given the multiyear latency of SSPE, additional cases might emerge over coming years. Reported measles history could not be established in one quarter of patients. Strengthened measles surveillance and sustained 2-dose vaccination coverage are needed.

title: Detection and Phylogenetic Characterization of Canine Distemper Virus (<i>Morbillivirus canis</i>) in Wild Foxes and Badgers from Northern Italy in 2021-2026
summary: Canine distemper virus (CDV) is a highly contagious multisystemic pathogen posing severe threats to wild carnivores and domestic animals. To investigate CDV circulation and lineage diversity in Piacenza Province, Northern Italy, wildlife surveillance was conducted under the Regional Wildlife Monitoring Plan between 2021 and June 2026. Forty-three wild carnivores-comprising red foxes (Vulpes vulpes), European badgers (Meles meles), wolves (Canis lupus), stone martens (Martes foina), and one jackal (Canis aureus)-were evaluated by necropsy, histopathology and molecular assays (RT-qPCR/RT-PCR). Overall, 12 animals (27.9%, 95% CI: 15.3-43.7; six foxes and six badgers) were confirmed to be CDV-positive. No positivity was found before 2024. Positive animals displayed characteristic lesions, including hemorrhagic enteritis, pulmonary hepatization, and footpad hyperkeratosis. Sequencing of the hemagglutinin (H) gene of the four complete H genes obtained revealed that they belonged to clade A of the European/South American 1 lineage, showing the highest nucleotide identity with Alpine CDV strains from Switzerland and Northern Italy. These results confirm the recent circulation of CDV amongst foxes and badgers in Piacenza. Continuous molecular monitoring and integrated cross-border surveillance remain essential for the effective management of transmission at the interface between wildlife and domestic animals.

title: Clinicopathologic Characteristics, Molecular Profile, Treatment, and Recurrence in Endometrial Cancer with Pelvic Lymph Node Isolated Tumor Cells
summary:
Objective

Our objective was to characterize the molecular-pathologic profile and recurrence patterns of endometrial cancer with pelvic lymph node isolated tumor cells (ITCs).

Methods

A single-center retrospective study of patients with endometrial cancer and ITCs was conducted. Patients with concurrent lymph nodes or distant metastasis were excluded. Cases were reviewed by a gynecologic pathologist, and electronic medical records were reviewed. Descriptive statistics were performed using R 4.4.2.

Results

A total of 43 patients were included, with a median follow-up time of 33 months. The majority were endometrioid carcinoma (91%) and stage I (72%). In total, 28 (65%) were MMR-proficient and p53-wild-type (MMRp p53wt), nine (21%) were MMR-deficient (MMRd), six (14%) were p53-abnormal (p53abn), and none were POLE-mutated (POLEmut). Additionally, 27 (96%) MMRp p53wt cases showed a microcystic, elongated, and fragmented (MELF) pattern of invasion. Adjuvant therapy was indicated in 38 (88%) patients; 32 (74%) received therapy and six (14%) declined. Four (9.3%) patients recurred, with a recurrence rate of 33% (2/6) for p53abn, 11% (1/9) for MMRd, and 4% (1/28) for MMRp p53wt. All recurrences were to distant sites. In the MMRp p53wt group, 16 (57%) had external beam radiation (EBRT) +/- vaginal brachytherapy (VBT), three (11%) had chemotherapy +/- radiation, and nine (32%) had no adjuvant treatment or VBT alone.

Conclusions

Molecular profile is prognostically relevant in endometrial carcinoma with ITCs. ITCs in MMRp p53wt endometrioid carcinoma present a low risk of disease recurrence. As the majority of our cohort received adjuvant therapy, future work may explore de-escalating treatment in low-risk ITC cases.

title: Real-world outcomes of asciminib versus first- and second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors as second-line treatment for chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia
summary:
Background

This study compared real-world outcomes of patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase (CML-CP) treated with asciminib and first/second generation (1 G/2 G) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) as second-line treatment (2 L) in the US.

Methods

A retrospective panel-based chart review from oncologists/hematologists was conducted on adult patients with CML-CP in 2 L treated with asciminib or 1 G/2 G TKIs between January 2022-June 2023 (index period). Entropy balancing was used to adjust baseline characteristics between asciminib and 1 G/2 G TKI cohorts. Time to discontinuation, progression to accelerated phase/blast crisis (AP/BC), BCR::ABL1 ≤ 0.1% (MMR), and BCR::ABL1 ≤ 0.01% (MR4) post-index were assessed using weighted Kaplan-Meier analyses and Gehan-Breslow tests.

Results

De-identified data on 255 patients (median age: 62.0, female: 43.5%, White: 56.1%) in the asciminib cohort were collected from 76 physicians (community/academic: 47.4/52.6%) and 233 patients (median age: 62.0, female: 43.3%, White: 56.2%) in the 1 G/2 G TKI cohort from 72 physicians (community/academic: 41.7/58.3%). By 48 weeks post-index, fewer patients in the asciminib (4.6%) versus 1 G/2 G TKI (10.4%) cohort experienced discontinuations (p = 0.07), and no patients progressed to AP/BC in the asciminib versus 4.2% in the 1 G/2 G TKI cohort (p < 0.05). By 48 weeks post-index, 68.3% of the asciminib versus 59.8% of the TKI cohort achieved or maintained MMR, and 40.6% versus 22.0% for MR4. Median time to MMR (MR4) was 30.7 (59.7) and 39.7 (72.7) weeks for the asciminib and 1 G/2 G TKI cohorts, respectively (all p < 0.05).

Conclusions

Findings from this large real-world US study suggest that 2 L asciminib offers favorable tolerability and better effectiveness compared with 1 G/2 G TKIs for patients with CML-CP.

title: Childhood immunisation default rate and its associated factors among children attending public health clinics in Klang Health District, Selangor, Malaysia: A cross-sectional study
summary: Childhood immunisation is one of the World Health Organization's strategies for reducing vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs). However, a proportion of children in Malaysia remain unvaccinated, as reflected in the increasing incidence of VPDs. This study aimed to determine the childhood immunisation default rate (CIDR) and its associated factors among children in Klang District. A cross-sectional study was conducted from July to September 2023 among parents or guardians accompanying children aged 12-24 months at selected maternal and child health clinics in Klang Health District. Systematic random sampling was used, and an assisted validated questionnaire was utilised to assess sociodemographic, immunisation and associated factors. Data were analysed using SPSS version 29, involving three-level analysis (descriptive, bivariate (chi- square and Fisher's exact test) and multivariable logistic regression). A total of 400 respondents were recruited. The CIDR was 25.5%. The second measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine dose (22.1%) had the highest default rate, followed by the third pneumococcal vaccine dose (16.3%) and first MMR vaccine dose (14.3%). Child with younger age group (P=0.045) was found to be a risk factor, whereby healthy children (P<0.001) and having no transportation (P<0.001) were the protective factors to defaulting. This study shows a high CIDR, reflecting gaps in existing policies and systems. Child's age, health status and transportation were significantly associated with the CIDR. Therefore, more awareness and knowledge about the contraindications for immunisation and the importance of correct timing for immunisation should be emphasis. The associations between immunisations defaulting and transportation availability warrants further investigations.

title: Evaluation of Vaccination Coverage and Compliance Among Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Documentary Analysis
summary: Vaccination is a cornerstone of primary healthcare, particularly critical for medical students and healthcare professionals due to constant occupational exposure to infectious agents. This study aimed to evaluate the vaccination status of medical students at a private higher education institution in the Federal District, Brazil, comparing their self-perceived protection with actual immunization records. A cross-sectional, descriptive study was conducted between August 2024 and July 2025, involving 90 medical students from various semesters. Data collection utilized structured online questionnaires and documentary analysis of digital vaccination cards submitted via the "Meu SUS Digital" platform or physical records. Evaluated immunizations included hepatitis A, hepatitis B (HBV), measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR), tetanus/dT, yellow fever, meningococcal C and ACWY, influenza (2024 campaign), and COVID-19. Data were analyzed using absolute and relative frequencies. Although 75 (83.3%) participants self-reported having an up-to-date vaccination card and 85 (94.4%) felt protected for clinical practice, documentary analysis revealed severe gaps. Only 16 (19.3%) participants possessed a completely up-to-date occupational schedule for all analyzed immunogens. Significant deficits included 56 (67.5%) lacking hepatitis A doses, 77 (92.8%) lacking meningococcal ACWY records, and 22 (26.5%) lacking the 2024 influenza vaccine. The primary reasons cited for missing vaccines were lack of availability at the appropriate age (n = 10, 43.5%) and unknown causes (n = 10, 43.5%). Descriptively, students with parents in the healthcare field and those in advanced internship semesters showed proportionally higher completeness rates, although overall coverage remained insufficient. Furthermore, 57 (63.3%) respondents recognized a lack of information regarding occupational infection risks during their academic training. A profound discrepancy exists between medical students' perceived immunological protection and their actual immunization status. These findings highlight an urgent need for institutional interventions, curriculum enhancements, and mandatory vaccination verification protocols to safeguard students and patients in clinical learning environments.

title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice and policy
summary: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

title: Prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance levels and childhood rubella incidence up to age 6 years: the Japan Environment and Children's Study
summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have raised concerns about their potential immunosuppressive effects. However, the association between prenatal PFAS exposure and childhood rubella remains unclear. This study examined whether prenatal PFAS exposure is associated with childhood rubella incidence. We analyzed data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study, including children whose mothers had plasma PFAS concentrations measured during pregnancy. The primary outcome was caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed rubella up to 6 years of age. Seven PFAS with detection frequencies >60% were analyzed. Logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate associations between PFAS concentrations and rubella incidence. Age-stratified analyses were performed, mixture effects were evaluated using quantile g-computation, and a nested case-control sensitivity analysis using conditional logistic regression was conducted. Of 25,253 eligible children, 15,694 were included after excluding non-first-born children from multiple births and participants with missing data; 43 had caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed rubella. No significant associations were observed between maternal PFAS concentrations and childhood rubella incidence in either the regression or age-stratified analyses. Mixture exposure analyses also showed no significant association, and the nested case-control sensitivity analysis yielded similar findings. In conclusion, we did not find a statistically significant association between maternal PFAS exposure during pregnancy and childhood rubella incidence up to 6 years of age. However, the limited number of rubella cases reduced statistical power to detect modest associations, and larger studies are warranted.

title: Predictive Performance of Inflammatory Markers for Severe Disease Progression in Measles: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis
summary: The recent European measles resurgence has driven record-high hospitalization, yet objective tools for early risk stratification remain scarce. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of routine admission inflammatory biomarkers for predicting severe disease and prolonged hospitalization. We retrospectively analyzed 509 patients with laboratory-confirmed measles hospitalized during a Romanian outbreak (November 2023-August 2025). Severe disease was defined via a clinical composite endpoint (intensive-care admission, mechanical ventilation, supplemental oxygen, acute respiratory failure, or sepsis). Biomarker discriminative performance was assessed using receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, Youden-optimal cut-offs, and DeLong tests. Multivariable logistic and Cox proportional-hazards regression evaluated independent predictors of severity and time to discharge. The cohort exhibited a pediatric predominance (median age: 3.0 years; 20% infants) with an 82% unvaccinated rate; 33% developed severe disease. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) demonstrated superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.863, 95% CI 0.820-0.898; cut-off ≥ 7 pg/mL, sensitivity 73%, specificity 93%), significantly outperforming ferritin (AUC 0.800) and conventional markers (all p < 0.001). Multivariable modeling established IL-6 and ferritin as the sole independent predictors of severity. All intensive-care admissions occurred exclusively for unvaccinated patients (5.0% vs. 0%). Severe disease, pneumonia, male sex, unvaccinated status and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) independently predicted prolonged hospitalization. Admission IL-6 and ferritin serve as robust, independent prognostic biomarkers that accurately identify high-risk measles patients, providing objective criteria with which to optimize clinical triage and inpatient management during outbreaks.

title: Molecular Profiles, Treatment-Associated Survival, and Prognosis in Early-Onset Versus Late-Onset Gastric Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
summary: Background: Whether early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a distinct clinical entity requiring age-specific management remains uncertain. We synthesized molecular profiles, treatment-associated survival, and prognosis to determine what current evidence supports in practice and requires prospective validation. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered, PRISMA-compliant review searched four databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and the Cochrane Library) from 1990 to 2025. Random-effects models compared EOGC with late-onset gastric cancer (LOGC) using each study's reported age definition, provided that the upper age cutoff for EOGC did not exceed 50 years, and evaluated treatment-survival associations within EOGC. Robustness was evaluated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and prediction intervals; certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Results: Fifty-eight studies involving 194,671 patients were included. EOGC showed lower observed odds of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) positivity (odds ratio [OR], 0.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-0.84) and microsatellite instability (MSI)/deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) positivity (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.91); p53 protein overexpression was less frequent, whereas the lower tumor protein p53 (TP53) mutation frequency represented only a non-significant numerical trend. E-cadherin loss was more frequent only under uniform immunohistochemical criteria (OR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.16-2.85). These largely unadjusted molecular estimates indicate prevalence patterns rather than independent age effects. Radical resection was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.37; 95% CI, 0.22-0.61), but confounding by indication and a prediction interval crossing unity precluded causal inference. The chemotherapy association was not retained under REML-Knapp-Hartung analysis. Evidence was insufficient to establish differences in overall, disease-free, or cancer-specific survival. Certainty was low to very low. Conclusions: Age alone does not justify altered biomarker testing, systemic treatment, or surveillance. This review distinguishes actionable practice from unsupported extrapolation: established biomarker testing should be applied irrespective of age, and young age should not deter assessment for curative-intent resection. It also defines the evidence standards required before any EOGC-specific stratification can be adopted.

title: A Case of Hidden Synchronous Colorectal Cancer
summary: Synchronous colorectal cancer (SCC) is uncommon and refers to multiple primary colorectal cancers arising simultaneously. The following case presents the clinical course of a 54-year-old female patient who presented with abdominal pain. She was found to have a mass in the hepatic flexure and another mass in the splenic flexure, both of which were found to be invasive adenocarcinoma and negative for mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency on the testing performed. Clinicians should be aware of SCC, as colonoscopy can identify tumors not visualized on computed tomography (CT), and early surgical intervention can ultimately be curative for patients.

title: Ectopic pregnancy-related severe maternal morbidity in Shenzhen: a sentinel indicator for gaps in early pregnancy care systems
summary:
Background

Despite China's progress in reducing maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity in early pregnancy, particularly ectopic pregnancy, remains a critical challenge in urban settings like Shenzhen. This study examines the clinical presentation scenarios, types, and sociodemographic compositions of ectopic pregnancy -related severe maternal morbidity to map potential structural vulnerabilities within the maternal healthcare continuum and propose interventions aligned with China's 'Healthy Motherhood 2030' agenda.

Methods

A retrospective analysis used 2023 data from Shenzhen's Maternal and Child Health Care Management Information System, covering 66 maternity hospitals. A total of 245 ectopic pregnancy-related severe maternal morbidity cases were identified using standard WHO near-miss criteria. Statistical analyses evaluated the descriptive distributions and baseline profiles of clinical outcomes across different initial resuscitation settings.

Results

Among 154,000 live births, 1,075 severe maternal morbidity cases (0.70%) included 257 (23.9%) ectopic pregnancy-related emergencies. After exclusions, we analysed 245 cases: 67.35% multiparous women, 31.84% had a junior high education or lower and 95% without prenatal care. Ectopic pregnancy-severe maternal morbidity occurred mostly at home (46.12%), followed by outpatient/emergency (30.20%) and inpatient (23.67%) settings. Among home/emergency presentations, 83.3% of women had lower education and 80.4% were employed. Tubal isthmus pregnancies (42.45%) dominated home-based emergencies, while atypical sites were frequent in clinical settings. Advanced severe complications occurred in only seven cases, limiting meaningful statistical comparisons across settings.

Conclusions

In a high-resource, low-MMR urban environment, ectopic pregnancy-related emergencies account for nearly one-quarter of the total SMM burden, with acute crises often concentrated in pre-hospital or frontline care settings. These descriptive patterns suggest that maternal safety strategies should consider shifting focus toward enhancing community health literacy and rapid-response integration at the primary care level. Forward-looking interventions - such as mobile health platforms, clinical simulation training, and formalised early pregnancy emergency networks - warrant prospective evaluation as potential operational pathways to bridge the identified gaps.

title: Factors associated with measles infection during the 2025-6 outbreak in Burao, Somaliland: a case-control study
summary:
Objectives

Somaliland has recurrent measles transmission, but outbreak-specific evidence on modifiable child, household, and health-service factors is limited. We examined factors associated with measles case status during the 2025-6 Burao outbreak.

Methods

We conducted a community-based unmatched case-control study among children aged <15 years from 14 June to 8 July 2026. Cases were enrolled consecutively and controls sampled systematically from households using a random start and every fourth household. Cluster-robust logistic regression estimated adjusted ORs (aORs), with indeterminate responses modeled separately.

Results

Among 804 children (290 cases, 514 controls), case status was associated with non-vaccination (aOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.02-4.42), close contact (3.00, 1.72-5.25), reported health-facility attendance (2.79, 1.91-4.06), vaccine unavailability (2.62, 1.17-5.85), and trucked/vendor water (2.98, 2.03-4.36). Prior malnutrition, large-gathering attendance, household vaccination-refusal history, and poor ventilation were also associated. Health-facility attendance referred to the 21 days before rash onset/reference date, but exact visit dates were not collected.

Conclusion

Measles case status was associated with immunity gaps, contact, household conditions, and service-related factors. Response priorities include reliable vaccine availability, catch-up vaccination, and contact-based action. The health-facility attendance association is temporally ambiguous and does not establish healthcare-associated transmission.

title: Immunoglobulin Use, Availability, and Administration Considerations in Measles Prevention
summary: In 2026, the National Foundation for Infectious Diseases (NFID), with the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), convened a Measles Summit in response to the largest U.S. measles resurgence in over three decades, with more than 3,000 confirmed cases mostly among unvaccinated individuals. Many clinicians and public health professionals have limited firsthand measles experience, underscoring the need for clinical guidance. In this commentary, we examine immune globulin (IG) use for measles post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) amid fragile supply and logistical challenges. GamaSTAN®, the sole Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-licensed intramuscular IG product, faces episodic availability, non-returnable single-vial economics, and a 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose, increasing per-patient demand. IVIG is increasingly employed when patients weigh 30 kg or more, beyond the weight at which an adequate dose of immune globulin can be given intramuscularly, or when IMIG supply is constrained, while concurrent lot withdrawals compromise institutional formularies. We review evidence-based patient selection for PEP, emphasizing that the Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccine remains first-line within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved when vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. Immunosuppressive therapies vary widely in their effects on the safety and efficacy of live vaccines. We therefore argue against categorizing every biologic, immunomodulator, or steroid as an automatic MMR contraindication, which would overestimate IG-PEP demand and preclude MMR for eligible patients. We propose class-specific stratification and an electronic health record decision-support rule to better align IG demand with genuine need. Finally, we address declining potency standards for measles antibody, attributable to waning donor titers, and offer guidance on dosing, multi-site pediatric administration, and infusion logistics within the PEP window.

title: Population-level measles RT-PCR cycle threshold values and their relationships with disease severity, transmission, and incidence metrics: a time series analysis of the 2025-2026 outbreak in Mexico
summary: To determine whether the weekly median real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) quantification cycle (Cq) value of notified measles cases precedes the incidence, transmission, and severity metrics of an outbreak. We focused particularly on the effective reproduction number (R t ). We also assessed whether any association persisted after adjustment for a linear time trend, specimen composition, and the outcome's own past. We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of 10,910 Cq determinations and 11,735 confirmed cases recorded in a single Mexican national case-level surveillance extract for Chihuahua and Jalisco. Twelve reported weekly metrics of incidence, transmission, and severity were examined by cross-correlation, four nested lagged regression models (M1-M4), formal Toda-Yamamoto Granger tests, and a secondary calibrated-lag autoregressive model. Moving-block bootstrap intervals were the primary method for regression inference. Autocorrelation-robust and classical methods were used in sensitivity analyses. Individual Cq determinations were analyzed separately against collection timing, severity, and vaccination history. Selected-lag associations were negative across all reported metric families, at leads of 1-9 weeks. The strongest negative correlation between Cq and DGE-derived R t occurred at +8 weeks in the second Chihuahua wave (r = -0.745). In Jalisco, it occurred at +7 weeks (r = -0.464). Only Jalisco supported the fully adjusted model 4 (M4). There, bootstrap intervals excluded zero for both the laboratory-positive-case and final surveillance-confirmed-case R t estimates but not for the two severity proportions. Excluding up to four endpoint weeks preserved the direction of both R t estimates. At the individual level, Cq increased with zero, one, and two documented vaccine doses (0.761 cycles per dose, 95% CI 0.589 to 0.932) and was 1.02 cycles lower in hospitalized cases. Aggregate Cq showed the most consistent retrospective leading association with R t . The retrospective associations occurred at data-calibrated lags of 7-8 weeks during the second Chihuahua wave and in Jalisco. Conversely, leak-free forecasting supported incremental gain in one analytic unit at a median 2-week horizon. The operational predictive horizon of aggregate Cq therefore remains unvalidated. If prospectively validated, weekly aggregate Cq could complement conventional measles surveillance using laboratory information that is already routinely collected.

title: Association Between Preoperative Nerve Conduction Study Severity and Outcomes After Open Carpal Tunnel Release
summary: Background Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common upper-extremity entrapment neuropathy for which nerve conduction studies (NCS) are widely used to confirm median neuropathy and characterize electrophysiological severity. However, the relationship between preoperative NCS severity and postoperative recovery following carpal tunnel release remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association between preoperative electrophysiological severity and six-month outcomes following open carpal tunnel release. Methods This prospective observational departmental audit included 60 consecutive adult patients with clinically and electrophysiologically confirmed CTS who underwent primary open carpal tunnel release at Kulhudhuffushi Regional Hospital, Maldives. Patients were categorized as having mild, moderate, or severe CTS according to preoperative NCS findings based on the Bland grading system. Outcomes included the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ), visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score, grip strength, patient satisfaction, and postoperative complications. Outcomes were assessed up to six months following surgery. Associations involving ordinal NCS severity were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation, while the relationship between distal motor latency and six-month BCTQ score was assessed using Pearson's correlation. Results The mean age of the 60 patients was 51.8 ± 10.6 years, and 42 (70.0%) were women. Sixteen patients (26.7%) had mild CTS, 28 (46.7%) had moderate CTS, and 16 (26.7%) had severe CTS. BCTQ and VAS scores improved significantly following surgery across all three severity groups. Six-month BCTQ scores differed significantly among the mild, moderate, and severe groups (1.45 ± 0.41, 1.81 ± 0.58, and 2.50 ± 0.80, respectively; F = 12.33; p < 0.001). Six-month VAS scores (F = 6.59; p = 0.003) and grip strength (F = 6.06; p = 0.004) also differed significantly among severity groups. However, the magnitude of improvement in BCTQ score did not differ significantly among the groups (p = 0.399). Longer symptom duration was associated with greater electrophysiological severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.479; p < 0.001), while greater preoperative distal motor latency was associated with a higher six-month BCTQ score (Pearson's r = 0.520; p < 0.001). Fifty patients (83.3%) were satisfied or very satisfied with their surgical outcome. Conclusions Open carpal tunnel release resulted in substantial symptomatic improvement across all preoperative electrophysiological severity groups. Greater preoperative NCS severity was associated with poorer absolute six-month patient-reported and functional outcomes, although the magnitude of symptomatic improvement was not significantly different among severity groups. Prolonged distal motor latency was moderately associated with higher residual BCTQ scores at six months. These findings suggest that preoperative NCS findings may provide useful prognostic information when counselling patients regarding expected recovery after carpal tunnel release.

title: Oncolytic measles virus reprograms the tumor microenvironment in a vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip model
summary: Background Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a rare and aggressive cancer primarily caused by asbestos exposure. Although dual immune checkpoint inhibition (anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4) is now approved as first-line therapy, clinical benefit is limited to a small subset of patients, necessitating the need for alternative strategies. Oncolytic viruses represent a promising therapeutic approach as they selectively infect and lyse tumor cells and display immunogenic properties. In PM, we showed that the oncolytic activity of measles virus (MV) is primarily dependent on alterations in the type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway. However, to date no in vitro models have yet been developed to mimic a sophisticated tumor microenvironment (TME), and accurately evaluate MV efficacy in PM. Methods We designed a humanized 3D “vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip” (VMOC) model using microfluidic chips that mimic a TME. VMOC are generated using primary endothelial cells, lung fibroblasts and patient-derived PM cells. We characterized the functionality of our model by confocal imaging, perfusion assay and single-cell RNA sequencing. The impact of MV on the VMOC was assessed by bulk transcriptomics, multiplex ELISA and deconvolution strategies, and compared to clinical data in patients with PM. Results We first proved VMOC functionality with an appropriate endothelial barrier integrity, perfusability, and vascular responsiveness to external stimuli. We demonstrated significant heterogeneity in the VMOC, with the presence of different mesenchymal, cancer and endothelial subpopulations. Interestingly, the addition of PM cells to the VMOC reduced both the IFN-I pathway in cells from the TME, and the abundance of a novel endothelial cell subset characterized by an IFN-I signaling signature. Following MV administration via the endothelial network, we detected PM cell infection and death, as well as strong activation of the IFN-I pathway with the production of multiple inflammatory mediators. Interestingly, the proteomic and transcriptomic inflammatory response induced by MV in VMOCs was similar to that induced in PM patients treated with an oncolytic virus. Conclusions The VMOC model we developed enables in vitro investigation of MV infection and TME reprogramming, paving the way for a deeper understanding of the TME role in OV responses and the development of novel strategies to improve clinical efficacy.

title: Interferon-induced OASL restricts ADAR1 p150 RNA binding and A-to-I RNA editing
summary:
ABSTRACT

The interferon (IFN)-inducible RNA editor ADAR1 p150 catalyzes adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing of host and viral double-stranded RNAs, limiting aberrant innate immune sensing and regulating gene expression. How ADAR1 p150 activity is regulated during host–virus interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the IFN-stimulated gene OASL as an inhibitor of ADAR1 p150. OASL engages p150 through two distinct interactions: its N-terminal OAS domain associates with the RNA-binding domains in an RNA-dependent manner, whereas its C-terminal ubiquitin-like domains bind the Zα domain independently of RNA. Despite their distinct canonical functions, the OAS and ubiquitin-like domains converge to limit ADAR1 p150 RNA binding and suppress A-to-I editing across the transcriptome. OASL also reverses p150-mediated suppression of antiviral and innate immune gene expression and counteracts p150-mediated enhancement of measles virus and vesicular stomatitis virus replication. Thus, OASL restrains ADAR1 p150, linking interferon signaling to the control of RNA editing and antiviral immunity.

title: MRI Utilisation in Acute Lateral Ankle Ligament Injuries: A Clinical Audit of Adherence to Evidence-Based Imaging Guidelines and Impact on Management
summary: Background Acute lateral ankle ligament injuries are common musculoskeletal presentations and are usually diagnosed through clinical assessment supported by plain radiography when indicated. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides detailed assessment of ligamentous, osteochondral, tendinous, and occult osseous pathology but is generally recommended selectively rather than routinely. Inappropriate or poorly justified MRI utilisation may increase resource use without altering clinical management. Objective To evaluate MRI utilisation in patients with acute lateral ankle ligament injuries at Kulhudhuffushi Regional Hospital, assess adherence to predefined evidence-based imaging criteria, identify deficiencies in clinical documentation, and determine whether appropriately indicated MRI was associated with changes in patient management. Methods A retrospective clinical audit was conducted at Kulhudhuffushi Regional Hospital, Maldives. Records of patients managed between February 1, 2025 and May 31, 2026 were reviewed. Fifty-five patients aged 14-65 years who presented within one to three weeks of acute traumatic ankle injury and underwent MRI for suspected lateral ankle ligament injury were included. Clinical documentation, plain radiographs, MRI reports, indications for MRI, and subsequent management were evaluated against predefined standards derived from international recommendations. MRI requests were classified as meeting evidence-based criteria when at least one recognised indication was documented before imaging; requests without a documented recognised indication were classified as potentially inappropriate. The association between MRI appropriateness and subsequent management change was evaluated using Fisher's exact test, with ORs and 95% CIs. Results All 55 patients (100%) underwent plain radiography before MRI. Forty-two MRI requests (76.4%) met predefined evidence-based indications, below the audit target of ≥90%, while 13 (23.6%) had no documented recognised indication and were classified as potentially inappropriate. Documentation was suboptimal for weight-bearing status (43, 78.2%), ligament-specific examination (37, 67.3%), syndesmotic testing (22, 40.0%), and the Ottawa Ankle Rules (16, 29.1%). Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) injury was the most frequent MRI finding, occurring in 32 patients (58.2%). Other findings included bone bruising in 11 (20.0%), combined ATFL and calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) injury in nine (16.4%), syndesmotic injury in six (10.9%), osteochondral lesions in four (7.3%), occult fractures in three (5.5%), and tendon injuries in three (5.5%). MRI resulted in a change in management in 19 patients (34.5%). Management changed in 18 of 42 patients (42.9%) whose MRI met evidence-based indications compared with one of 13 patients (7.7%) whose MRI lacked a documented recognised indication (OR: 9.00, 95% CI: 1.07-75.70; Fisher's exact test, p = 0.022). Conclusions MRI was most clinically useful when requested for patients with documented evidence-based indications. Although compliance with first-line plain radiography was complete, deficiencies were identified in clinical documentation and MRI selection. Appropriately indicated MRI was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of management change. A structured ankle assessment proforma, standardised MRI request criteria, improved rehabilitation pathways, and clinician education are proposed, followed by a re-audit to assess improvement.

title: Efficient host transmission of measles virus: disentangling misconceptions from established findings
summary: SUMMARYMeasles virus (MeV) is considered the most contagious human virus. This review critically examines explanations for MeV's extraordinary transmissibility. Although substantial progress has been made in understanding MeV infection, pathogenesis, and host spread, the fundamental question of why MeV is markedly more transmissible than other structurally similar respiratory viruses within the same taxonomic families remains unresolved. Many commonly cited explanations are either incorrect, oversimplified, or insufficiently supported by rigorous experimental evidence. Notably, there is a striking lack of studies that directly investigate the mechanisms governing MeV transmission. This knowledge gap persists in part because humans are the only natural reservoir for MeV, and thus the most relevant experimental models can be costly, technically challenging, and limited in ability. Moreover, studies addressing MeV environmental stability have relied largely on in vitro laboratory conditions that may have limited relevance to real-world transmission scenarios. While these studies have yielded useful observations, they often lack definitive mechanistic insight into efficient host-to-host spread. In this review, we discuss multiple strategies to investigate and define the efficient transmission of MeV, including (i) epidemiology, (ii) stability in controlled environments, (iii) infectious dose, (iv) incubation period, and (v) shedding from the respiratory epithelium. As will be discussed, quantitative, head-to-head comparisons of MeV transmission dynamics with those of other common respiratory viruses, such as influenza virus, rhinovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus, are notably absent. A clearer understanding of the mechanisms that govern efficient MeV transmission may inform strategies to reduce spread in educational, healthcare, and community settings.

title: Descriptive epidemiology of measles in the southern region of Afghanistan, 2024-2025: a secondary analysis from regional case-based surveillance data
summary:
Objectives

After a three-fold increase in measles outbreaks in Afghanistan during 2024, this study aimed to assess the descriptive epidemiology of measles in the southern region.

Methods

This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted on case-based measles surveillance data retrieved from the District Health Information System 2 for the period from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and immunization status data were summarized descriptively and surveillance system performance was assessed using World Health Organization indicators.

Results

Of 4379 suspected measles cases, 3346 (76.4%) were laboratory-confirmed and 52.7% were males. The median age was 24 months (interquartile range 12-60), and four-fifths were children aged under 5 years. A total of 66.5% of cases were from Kandahar; overall, 80.9% of all cases and 80.2% of confirmed cases did not have a measles-containing vaccine record. Helmand had the highest proportion of unvaccinated cases at 97.7%. The overall discarded rate was 10.55 per 100,000 population; the adequate time for investigation, specimen adequacy, laboratory receipt of specimen, and communication of results with public health authorities were 98.3%, 99.1%, 77.7%, and 82.8%, respectively.

Conclusion

Measles transmission in southern Afghanistan during 2024-2025 was predominantly recorded along with a large unvaccinated population for measles-containing vaccine, concentrated in children aged under 5 years, with highlighted provincial disparities in immunization and surveillance timeliness. Geographically differentiated responses prioritizing outreach vaccination and strengthening specimen transport in the lowest-performing provinces are urgently required.

title: Viral Infections and Ovarian Reserve: Mechanistic Insights into Ovarian Aging- A Review
summary: Ovarian aging, marked by the progressive loss of follicular reserve and decline in oocyte quality, is a principal determinant of female reproductive lifespan. While genetic and environmental factors are well-established contributors, viral infections, including both DNA and RNA viruses, are increasingly recognized as significant extrinsic modulators of ovarian function. This review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms and clinical outcomes by which key viral pathogens, such as severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), human papillomavirus (HPV), mumps virus, herpes simplex virus (HSV), and rubella virus, affect ovarian aging and reserve. The discussion highlights those viral infections can impact ovarian function through inflammation, cytopathic effects, oxidative stress, and immune-mediated mechanisms, although the magnitude and clinical relevance vary. Current evidence for viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 and HBV is limited and inconsistent, highlighting the need for individualized assessment when considering fertility interventions. Further longitudinal and mechanistic studies are essential to clarify long-term reproductive outcomes and to guide evidence-based fertility counseling.

title: The Impermanence of Public Health Gains-Lessons Learned from Measles Resurgence, Bangladesh, 2026
summary: The global resurgence of measles is a major public health concern. After the success of its Expanded Programme on Immunization, Bangladesh experienced a measles resurgence in 2026. The country faced major setbacks after measles vaccination coverage declined because of political instability, discontent among field-level staff, change in procurement policy, COVID-19-related service disruptions, and delayed supplementary immunization campaigns. During March 15-September 13, 2026, Bangladesh reported 170,638 suspected and 20,006 confirmed measles cases, including 919 deaths among suspected and 100 deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases. The outbreak disproportionately affected unvaccinated and underimmunized children. Political turmoil during 2024-2025 disrupted vaccine procurement, delayed mass vaccination campaigns, weakened the health workforce, and compromised financial and logistic continuity. Simultaneously, disruptions in vitamin A supplementation and worsening child malnutrition amplified disease severity. To prevent future resurgence, immunization programs must be depoliticized, supported by buffer vaccine stocks, strengthened through microlevel surveillance, and integrated with nutrition and primary healthcare services.

title: Tracking the impact of maternal health service coverage on maternal mortality across 137 low- and middle-income countries in the progress toward Sustainable Development Goals
summary:
Background

Achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, particularly targets 3.1 (reducing the global maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to less than 70 per 100,000 live births) and 3.8 (universal health coverage), requires sustained reductions in maternal mortality and equitable access to essential maternal health services (MHS). Despite global progress, large disparities persist. Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) account for more than 90% of maternal deaths worldwide, largely reflecting gaps in access to essential MHS. However, multi-country evidence examining how improvements in MHS during the SDG period translate to reductions in MMR remains limited. This study assessed disparities in MHS coverage and their associations with MMR across LMICs.

Methods

We conducted a longitudinal panel analysis of 137 LMICs, using country-level data from the World Health Organization Global Health Observatory and the World Bank from 2015 to 2023. Indicators included coverage of at least four antenatal care visits (ANC4+), facility-based delivery (FBD), and skilled birth attendance (SBA). We estimated associations between MHS coverage and MMR using generalised linear mixed models with a gamma-log link, with analyses stratified by country income group and maternal education.

Results

The median MMR of the 137 LMICs declined from 109.3 to 85.5 deaths per 100,000 live births from 2015 to 2023. Coverage of FBD and SBA increased by 5.6% and 5.0%, respectively. Higher coverage of ANC4+ (β = -0.01, P = 0.02) and FBD (β = -0.01, P = 0.03) was significantly associated with lower MMR. These associations were stronger in lower-middle-income and upper-middle-income countries than in low-income countries. Stratified analyses showed larger reductions in MMR among women with moderate-to-high levels of maternal education.

Conclusions

Although maternal mortality decreased during the SDG period, progress remains insufficient and inequitable. Strengthening equitable access to essential MHS is critical to accelerating MMR reductions and supporting progress toward SDG targets in LMICs.

title: Small quantity lipid-based nutritional supplementation and measles vaccination coverage in children aged 6-23 months: a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial
summary: Undernutrition and infectious diseases pose a double threat to child survival, especially in areas with a high malnutrition burden and low vaccination coverage. In this study, we evaluated whether distributing preventive small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) alongside routine immunization services may increase vaccine uptake in a pediatric, pragmatic, cluster-randomized controlled trial in northern Nigeria. Twenty geographically defined clusters across two Local Government Areas were randomized 1:1 to the NutriVax strategy (intervention) or standard National Program of Immunization (NPI) services (control). NutriVax provided a monthly ration of SQ-LNS to children aged 6-23 months after routine NPI delivery at primary healthcare centers. The primary outcome was coverage of the first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) verified by vaccination card among children aged 12-23 months, assessed in an endline population-based household cross-sectional survey 12 months after conducting a similar baseline survey. The endline survey included 1,604 children (801 control, 803 NutriVax); 48% of children surveyed in intervention clusters had ever received SQ-LNS. The odds of receiving card-verified MCV1 were two times higher in the NutriVax arm than in the control arm (odds ratio = 2.08, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.30-3.35, P = 0.004). The difference-in-differences, cluster conditional analysis indicated a 20.1 percentage-point (pp) increase in MCV1 coverage from baseline (95% CI: 13.7-26.5 pp, P < 0.0001) relative to the control arm. Co-delivering SQ-LNS with routine immunization substantially improved card-verified MCV1 uptake, supporting a scalable strategy to make progress toward targets set by the World Health Organization's Immunization Agenda 2030 in similar settings. title: Nationwide Surveillance and Control Measures during Large Measles Outbreak, Bangladesh, 2026
summary: Nationwide surveillance in Bangladesh during April 2-May 27, 2026, identified a total of 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed measles cases across 8 administrative divisions. Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Despite high reported vaccine coverage, transmission persisted amid residual immunity gaps. Vaccine stockouts, discontinued vaccination campaigns, and coverage overestimation likely contributed to Bangladesh's largest recorded measles outbreak.

title: Colorectal Cancer: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Signaling Pathways, Clinical Features, Screening, Diagnosis, and Management
summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality worldwide and is increasingly characterized by two converging realities: a substantial global burden and a rising incidence of early-onset CRC. This review synthesizes current advances in CRC epidemiology, risk factors, signaling biology, clinical presentation, screening, diagnosis, and management across the care continuum. We frame CRC as a systems-level disease in which genomic instability, epigenetic dysregulation, metabolic remodeling, tumor microenvironmental evolution, and gut microbiota interactions converge on interconnected pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-β, and immune-regulatory networks. We distinguish established standards of care from recent practice-changing developments and investigational strategies. Within this framework, we discuss blood-based screening, AI-assisted endoscopy, ctDNA-informed residual disease assessment, biomarker-defined molecular workup, immunotherapy strategies for dMMR disease, and targeted approaches for KRAS G12C-mutated, BRAF V600E-mutated, and HER2-positive metastatic CRC. Despite substantial progress, major challenges remain, including limited immunotherapy benefit in microsatellite-stable CRC, unequal access to high-quality screening and molecular testing, and uncertainty regarding implementation of newer biomarkers across diverse populations. An integrated framework linking population risk, tumor ecology, evidence-based biomarker use, and equitable precision care is essential for the next phase of CRC prevention and management.
